affiliations: Dalian University of Technology, Clemson University, Dalian University of Technology and The University of Hong Kong

detail.title: Mitigating Advertising Intrusiveness on Social Media platforms The Role of Heterogeneous Social Cues, Mechanisms, and Boundary Conditions
detail.abstract: While advertising is vital for social media platform, its intrusive nature can erode both marketing effectiveness and platform satisfaction. To mitigate intrusiveness, social newsfeed advertising (SNA) strategically integrates social cues—such as Likes, Shares, Ratings, and Sales—to blend commercial messages into organic interactions. However, prior research has not sufficiently explored how social cues mitigate SNA intrusiveness, especially regarding their heterogeneity, underlying mechanisms, and boundary conditions. Drawing on attitude function theory, this study investigates how distinct social cues (proximal vs. remote, action-based vs. attitude-based) mitigate SNA intrusiveness through sociability and informativeness. Two 5×2 between-subjects factorial experiments using a self-developed system show that proximal cues are more effective for social products and high self-monitors by enhancing sociability, whereas remote cues benefit utilitarian products and low self-monitors by boosting informativeness. Moreover, attitude-based cues foster sociability, while action-based cues promote informativeness, leading to differential intrusiveness mitigation. These findings establish a taxonomy of social cues, clarify their mechanisms and boundary conditions, and offer practical guidance for platforms and marketers to design less intrusive SNA.

detail.title: From Skepticism to Trust: Factors That Mitigate Greenwashing Perceptions
detail.abstract: The concept of a Green World was introduced in 1972 during a UN Conference. The concept has significantly influenced business practices aimed at environmental protection. Lot of business firms started altering their practices to comply with the concept of green world. The phenomena of greenwashing emerged while firms falsely claimed green practices without doing efforts to protect the environment from the adversities of their business operations. This led to consumer skepticism and altered buying decisions. On the other hand, certain firms faced greenwashing perceptions among their customers while the firms were (actually) following eco-friendly practices. This study addresses the prevention of greenwashing perceptions among Generation-Z customer residing in urban areas of the country. Utilizing the business websites and customer responses; this research explores the link of Greenwashing Perceptions with Green Information Quality, Environmental Communication, Green Transparency, Brand Credibility and Pro Environmental Behaviour. Cross-sectional survey method has been used for data collection. Correlation and regression analysis have been made using structural equation modelling for obtaining empirical results. The framework of the study is based on several previous studies conducted on the antecedents of greenwashing perceptions. The study contributes to societal wellbeing and addresses the organizational challenges by suggesting measures to prevent greenwashing perceptions which ultimately support sustainable practices and improve customer trust.

detail.abstract: We test for time variation in the slope of the US Phillips curve exploiting the post-COVID inflation episode as a quasi-experimental setting. To do so, we leverage data on inflation and unemployment across US metropolitan statistical areas (MSAs) and use a two-region New-Keynesian model to derive the slope of the aggregate Phillips curve from our MSA-level estimates. We find that the slope of the Phillips curve increased substantially during the post-COVID inflation and disinflation periods, reaching its highest level since the mid-1970s. We further examine the mechanisms suggested by our model and document that a sizable estimated decrease in the elasticity of labor supply and the post-COVID increase in the frequency of price change jointly account for the Phillips curve steepening.

detail.title: Unemployment Volatility and Wage Dispersion with Optimal Incentive Contracts
detail.abstract: We develop a two-stage calibration method for search models. In the first stage, without the need to specify how wages are determined, we show that in order to generate the observed large unemployment volatility, it’s both necessary and sufficient for the profit elasticity with respect to productivity to be above a lower bound. In the second stage, we show that optimal incentive contracts can account for unemployment volatility and wage dispersion simultaneously, even when the value of non-market activity is procyclical and wages are flexible. Moreover, it is shown that unemployment insurance can increase output by encouraging more socially-efficient contracts.

detail.abstract: Street begging remains a persistent socioeconomic challenge in South Asia, closely linked to unemployment, poverty, lack of education, and weak social safety nets. This paper explores an integrated model combining rescue, rehabilitation, skill development, and community-driven enterprises to address the crisis. detail.title: Visual Persuasion Reloaded: Exploring the Impact of Television Ads on Buying Behaviour in Tamil Nadu through Structural Equation Modelling (SEM)
detail.abstract: In the evolving landscape of consumerism, television commercials continue to play a crucial role in shaping buying behaviour-even in this digitally driven e-commerce era. This empirical study examines the multidimensional impact of television advertisements on consumer purchase decisions across selected districts of Tamil Nadu. Drawing from a sample of 800 respondents, the research investigates how key advertising elements-such as information content, creativity, logic, music, lyrics, punchlines, and celebrity appeal-influence consumer perception and motivation. A Structural Equation Model (SEM) was developed to explore the relationships among latent constructs: Ad Content Appeal, Aesthetic Stimuli, Celebrity Influence, Perception, Motivation, and Buying Behaviour. The study provides theoretical and practical insights for marketers and advertisers aiming to optimize television advertising strategies in an era where digital and traditional media coexist. The validated SEM underscores the continued relevance of TV commercials and their underlying psychological triggers in influencing modern consumer decisions.

title: DeFRCN-PF: Mitigating Knowledge Forgetting in Few-Shot Object Detection via Class Proxy
affiliations: Central China Normal University, Central China Normal University and California State University Fullerton

detail.title: DeFRCN-PF: Mitigating Knowledge Forgetting in Few-Shot Object Detection via Class Proxy
detail.abstract: The primary task of Few-Shot Object Detection (FSOD) is to detect new objects from previously unseen classes rapidly. FSOD is widely used to handle scenarios with limited data. However, while most works focus solely on the performance for novel classes, detecting all classes is crucial for practical applications where test data may contain any instance. This necessitates that few-shot detectors mitigate the forgetting of knowledge about base classes as much as possible. To address the problem of knowledge forgetting, which impairs detection performance on base classes, this paper proposes a detection model named DeFRCN-PF, based on the DeFRCN framework. The model introduces an innovative class-proxy module to store and consolidate the knowledge representations of base classes. Furthermore, it designs a dynamic weight fusion mechanism to integrate the base-class memory adaptively with novel-class predictions during inference.Extensive experiments were conducted on the PASCAL VOC and MS COCO datasets based on the Generalized Few-Shot Object Detection (G-FSOD) benchmark. The experimental results show that on the PASCAL VOC dataset under the 10-shot setting, DeFRCN-PF improves the mean Average Precision (AP) by 1.2 percentage points compared to the DeFRCN baseline, while maintaining high detection performance on novel classes. On the MS COCO dataset, the novel AP (nAP) is improved by 1.23 percentage points, demonstrating that the model mitigates knowledge forgetting while enhancing the detection performance for novel classes.

detail.title: Generalized Bayesian subset simulation for the evaluation of failure probability
detail.abstract: Evaluation of failure probability is essential in system design and analysis. But it has become increasing prohibitive due to growing system complexity and soaring simulation costs. To address such challenge, we propose a novel active learning framework, the generalized Bayesian subset simulation (GBSS), to estimate failure probability. Based on the concept of generalized subset simulation, GBSS introduces a novel threshold-first criteria and decomposes the target failure events into an optimal sequence of intermediate events. Combined with a Bayesian surrogate model, high-quality conditional samples may be generated efficiently with residual resampling in Markov chain Monte Carlo and in turn improves model accuracy. We evaluate our framework via a comprehensive set of academic examples and industrial cases of high dimensions. Comparing to four state-of-the-art methods, including Monte Carlo, subset simulation, generalized subset simulation and multi-fidelity subset simulations, GBSS demonstrates substantial improvements in both numerical efficiency and stability.

detail.title: Multi-Phase, Multi-Generation Pricing Optimization model for New and Remanufactured Short-Lived Products considering consumers' Behavioral effects
detail.abstract: This paper investigates optimal pricing strategies for new and remanufactured short-lived products, such as smartphones and laptops, where multiple generations of such products coexist. The study employs a surplus function-based approach to models and examines the effect of consumer behavior and market dynamics on the optimal price of the product. Under consumer behavior, we study the impact of contrast, assimilation effects, and green consumerism on price. We also study market dynamics such as product differentiation and generational effects. While validating several extant findings, the study converges upon several novel insights. For instance, the research highlights that strong contrast and weaker assimilation effects tend to equalize the prices of both old and new generations of products. The study has important implications for research streams like pricing, timing of product launch, and remanufacturing.

title: From vision to value: Stock chart image-driven factors and their pricing power
affiliations: Hanyang University, Hanyang University and Hanyang University

detail.title: From vision to value: Stock chart image-driven factors and their pricing power
detail.abstract: This paper investigates whether stock chart image–based deep learning models uncover priced risk factors that extend beyond the established factor zoo. Factors are constructed from predictions of a Vision Transformer (ViT) and a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and evaluated within a stochastic discount factor (SDF) framework using double-selection LASSO against 161 benchmark factors. Portfolio tests reveal that the ViT factor generates robust return spreads across firm sizes and achieves superior risk-adjusted performance, with Sharpe and Sortino ratios exceeding the market benchmark. In contrast, the CNN factor demonstrates limited economic relevance, showing significance primarily in small- and micro-cap stocks. SDF loading analysis confirms that both image-driven factors are statistically significant; however, only the ViT factor translates this statistical strength into meaningful economic value. These findings establish that advanced visual pattern recognition, specifically through ViT architectures, captures a novel priced dimension of risk not spanned by conventional factors. The results highlight the potential of chart-based signals as a complementary source of information for empirical asset pricing.

detail.title: L’atomo fuggente: analisi di un possibile ritorno al nucleare in Italia (The Prodigal Atom: An Analysis on the Potential Comeback of Nuclear Power in Italy)

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of Italy Occasional Paper No. 947

detail.abstract:
Italian Abstract: Il dibattito su una possibile reintroduzione del nucleare nel mix energetico nazionale si è recentemente riaperto. Questo lavoro riprende lo studio di Faiella e Lavecchia (2012) per valutare le conseguenze che potrebbe avere in termini di riduzione del prezzo dell’elettricità, della dipendenza energetica e delle emissioni di gas serra, offrendo ulteriori elementi di valutazione e riflessione anche alla luce dei cambiamenti degli ultimi anni. Dall’analisi emerge che, dati la struttura del mercato e della bolletta elettrica, una reintroduzione del nucleare non avrebbe significativi impatti sul livello dei prezzi. Piuttosto, potrebbe ridurne la volatilità, contribuendo a stabilizzare la spesa per l’elettricità per i sottoscrittori di contratti a lungo termine. Sul fronte della dipendenza energetica, la riduzione delle importazioni di idrocarburi sarebbe compensata da una maggiore importazione della tecnologia e del combustibile per la produzione nucleare, in questo momento concentrati in paesi geo-politicamente poco affini all’Italia. Il contributo di una reintroduzione del nucleare alla riduzione delle emissioni di gas serra è invece potenzialmente consistente. Un altro elemento importante che emerge dall’analisi sono le incertezze legate alle tecnologie scelte, gran parte delle quali non sono ancora disponibili per la commercializzazione. Tali incertezze rendono opportuno un approccio cauto, che predisponga e promuova anche strategie alternative.

English Abstract: The debate about the possibility of reintroducing nuclear power into the national energy mix has recently been reopened. This paper builds on the study by Faiella and Lavecchia (2012), offering further points for reflection, particularly in light of recent changes. It aims to assess the potential consequences of a nuclear comeback on electricity prices, energy dependence and greenhouse gas emissions. The analysis shows that, given the current market structure and the composition of electricity bills, reintroducing nuclear power would not have a significant impact on price levels. However, it could reduce its volatility, helping to stabilize electricity expenditure for long-term contract subscribers. In terms of energy dependence, the reduction in hydrocarbon imports would be offset by the increased import of the technology and fuel required for nuclear production. These resources are currently concentrated in countries with a high level of geopolitical risk. The reintroduction of nuclear power would contribute significantly to reducing greenhouse gas emissions. The analysis also shows that there are still some uncertainties around the selected technologies, as most of them are not yet commercially viable. These uncertainties highlight the need to develop and promote alternative strategies.

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of Greece Economic Bulletin, Issue 61

detail.abstract: This paper evaluates the effectiveness of Value Added Tax (VAT) reductions as a tool to mitigate inflation in Greece, combining empirical evidence with structural macroeconomic analysis. First, the estimation of a small-scale structural vector autoregression (SVAR) model reveals that temporary VAT reductions exert a statistically insignificant effect on inflation. Nevertheless, when VAT reductions are accompanied by enhancements in product market competition, the disinflationary effects become both significant and persistent. Second, the results from a Dynamic Stochastic General Equilibrium (DSGE) model calibrated to the Greek economy indicate that the short-run pass-through of VAT cuts to consumer prices is partial, ranging between 19% and 25% in the short term. This pass-through is highly influenced by structural factors and the persistence of policy interventions. Notably, permanent VAT cuts generate nearly twice the inflation passthrough compared to temporary ones. The disinflationary impact is also stronger in economies with more competitive product markets, where firms are more likely to transmit cost reductions to prices. Conversely, in economies characterised by relatively high nominal rigidities or limited domestic input use, the inflation response to VAT reductions is diminished. Overall, the results of the study demonstrate the significance of structural conditions in determining the inflationary outcomes of VAT-based fiscal measures.

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of Italy Occasional Paper No. 948

detail.abstract: We show that sustainable investment by mutual funds influences non-financial firms’ stock prices and real outcomes. Our identification exploits the EU Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation (SFDR) – requiring mutual funds to disclose no, mild, or strong commitment to sustainable investment – and rich microdata. Funds disclosing a mild commitment reduce exposure to high ESG risk (‘brown’) stocks, relative to those with no commitment. By contrast, strongly committed funds do not adjust, being already perceived as sustainable and having little incentive to further signal their ESG strategy. The divestment of brown firms occurs independently of their prior sustainability pledges and reduces their stock prices. This reduction is in turn associated with lower environmental spending and higher carbon emissions. Our findings suggest that blanket divestment by ESG funds may unintentionally worsen environmental performance by weakening firms’ incentives to invest in sustainability.

Italian Abstract: Dopo un lungo periodo di divergenza, nell’ultimo quinquennio l’economia meridionale è tornata a crescere a tassi superiori a quelli del Centro Nord. La ripresa economica ha coinciso con alcuni segnali di rafforzamento del tessuto produttivo e delle condizioni di contesto in cui le imprese operano. English Abstract: After a long period of divergence, over the past five years, the Southern Italian economy has resumed growing at a faster pace than the Centre-North. The economic recovery has been accompanied by some signs of strengthening in the production system and in the business environment. However, the gap in per capita income with the Centre-North remains exceptionally wide. In addition to documenting the current extent of the regional divide across multiple dimensions, this paper offers insights into and quantitative analyses on some of the development prospects for the Southern Italian economy.

detail.title: The Silver Crest Mine

publicationDetails.journalName: Darden Case Collection

detail.abstract:
In this case, students explore decision-making under uncertainty and apply dynamic programming (DP), a powerful tool for optimizing sequential decisions. Set in the context of the ore mining industry, the case revolves around a strategic auction for a 10-year lease of the Silver Crest Mine (Silver Crest), recently reopened due to a rise in silver prices. Two firms—TerraGold and MineralCorp—are the sole qualified bidders. The auction winner secures exclusive rights to operate the mine for the next decade and can make annual decisions on whether to keep the mine open or close it down. Silver produced during any operational year is sold at that year's prevailing market price, which is highly volatile and follows a stochastic process.The central challenge lies in valuing the lease. To do so, each firm must account not only for the expected future trajectory of silver prices but also for the irreversible fixed costs of opening and closing the mine. Further, MineralCorp benefits from access to a high-efficiency continuous miner, which reduces its per-ounce operating cost, while TerraGold possesses advanced analytical expertise and leverages DP to construct an operating policy adaptable to evolving market conditions. Working from TerraGold's perspective, students develop a bidding strategy informed by dynamic optimization.At the University of Virginia Darden School of Business, this case is used in the Executive MBA core Decision Analysis course as part of a three-session module on DP. It can be taught in a core course in Decision Analysis or Business Analytics, or as part of an elective on Optimization or Quantitative Methods for Management. In all settings, we strongly recommend using this case with the companion technical note, “Introduction to Dynamic Programming” (UVA-QA-0955).

Excerpt

The Silver Crest Mine

In 2023, eight years after closing operations in the Silver Crest Mine (Silver Crest), the current owners of Silver Crest decided to lease out the mine in reaction to the recent uptick in silver prices. A stringent bidding process was put in place to decide the next mine operator, and MineralCorp and TerraGold were the only two companies that met the requirements to participate in the bidding. The highest bidder in a sealed-price auction would win the rights to operate the mine for the next 10 years. At the end of the 10 years, the mine would revert to the lessor “as is,” with no obligation by the lessee to have the mine in operation or idle prior to the expiration of the lease. The minimum bidding price was $1 million.

Silver Crest dated back to the silver rush of the late 1800s, when the mine was discovered in a remote region known for its rich and abundant mineral deposits. A combination of economic challenges, environmental concerns, and operational difficulties led to its closure in 2015. The prevailing factor behind the mine's closure was a protracted period of low silver prices that rendered operations economically unviable.

With a track record of employing state-of-the-art mining equipment, MineralCorp possessed an idle continuous miner that it could conveniently put to use if the company were to win the lease, allowing it to streamline operations. On the other hand, TerraGold, a rising star in the industry, had developed a reputation for its expertise in optimizing manual drilling and blasting.

detail.title: Values Primacy & Total Governance Through Activism

publicationDetails.detailsText: SMU Dedman School of Law Legal Studies Research Paper No. 699

detail.abstract:
In the aftermath of George Floyd’s murder, public companies swiftly pledged sweeping equity commitments—only to abandon them under political and market pressure. These reversals were not aberrations. They were opportunistic, performative, and reactionary marketing responses. They expose a governance regime in which stakeholder interests are structurally reversible because they remain doctrinally optional—lacking the institutional interlock needed to create binding accountability across stakeholder roles. 

This Article explores how stakeholder power is already embedded in corporate governance through interlocking initiatives grounded in shared values. Stakeholder activism—boycotts, proxy votes, viral campaigns—is not merely expressive; it is an overlooked form of governance. Drawing on fiduciary doctrine, collective action theory, law and political economy, and governance models, this Article blurs the boundary between private enterprise and public governance. It shows how Total Governance enables ordinary individuals to coordinate across roles—employee, consumer, investor, community member—and exert influence regardless of whether they contribute capital. 

Taken seriously, Total Governance challenges the assumption that governance power belongs only to capital. When stakeholders identify and act on shared values and superordinate goals, they exert real institutional power—not from within the boardroom, but through coordinated civic action. Total Governance is not an aspiration; it is a structural fact. What appears to be reputational noise is, in fact, governance at work.

Through case studies of Target, Tesla, and Meta, we show how activism shapes corporate outcomes in real time—and how cross-role coordination can impose binding constraints on firm identity. The structural geometries of the corporate form—ownership concentration, platform embeddedness, and transition costs—condition how Total Governance emerges, fragments, or consolidates. Total Governance helps explain how civic accountability endures even as legal structures—via charter competition, private equity opacity, and shareholder disenfranchisement—increasingly insulate corporate power from constraint. 

This Article argues that legitimacy no longer stems from boardroom deliberation alone, but from civic accountability forged in public struggle. By exposing the porous boundary between public pressure and private governance, it redefines the power of everyday individuals to govern corporate enterprise—especially consumer-facing firms operating at public scale.

title: Impact of Interprofessional and Interagency Collaboration in U.S. Child Welfare Systems: A Scoping Review
affiliations: University of Connecticut, University of Connecticut, University of Georgia and Michigan State University

detail.title: Impact of Interprofessional and Interagency Collaboration in U.S. Child Welfare Systems: A Scoping Review
detail.abstract: Background: Collaboration among child welfare providers and agencies is considered critical in child welfare, but the extant literature lacks a systematic, comprehensive review of studies examining how they impact clients and professionals. Objective: To review the nature and extent of studies of outcomes associated with collaboration in U.S. child welfare systems.Methods: We conducted a scoping review of the peer-reviewed and grey literature. Studies had to be in English and U.S.-based to be included. Results: Sixty-nine of 4,535 studies screened met inclusion criteria. Included studies examined 15 components of collaboration and 20 types of professionals or agencies. Nineteen studies used a theory, model, framework, or perspective. Studies used quantitative, qualitative, and mixed methods approaches, but only 8 included a comparison or control group. Sixty-seven percent measured collaboration—most using a single item and self-report measures. Studies explored 81 client outcomes related to safety, permanency, wellbeing, service access and availability, timeliness and efficiency, service quality, engagement and motivation. Additionally, the literature addressed 82 professional outcomes related to casework practices, knowledge, support, wellbeing, performance, and legal proceedings. Most studies found that collaboration led to better outcomes, although findings client outcomes were more variable than professional outcomes. Conclusions: The literature provides a multifaceted understanding of how collaboration may impact clients and professionals in child welfare, but more studies with strong conceptual foundations and rigorous research designs are needed. Further research should also be conducted to clarify which components of collaboration are most critical and which outcomes are influenced by collaboration.

detail.title: Unpacking Leadership Competency–Performance Pathways: Jd–R and Full-Range Leadership Perspectives on Engagement and Culture in an Emerging Market
detail.abstract: Leadership competency (LC) is recognized as a key driver of business performance (BP), yet its mechanisms in emerging markets remain underexplored. Drawing on the Job Demands–Resources model, Full-Range Leadership Theory, and Resource-Based View, this study tests employee engagement (EE) and organizational culture (OC) as mediators in the LC–BP link, and transformational (TL) and transactional leadership (TxL) as moderators within Ethiopia’s high power-distance banking sector. Data from 581 mid- and senior-level managers across 17 commercial banks (87% response rate) were analyzed using structural equation modeling and PROCESS macro (Models 1, 4, 58). Findings confirm significant direct and mediated effects of LC on BP through EE and OC, with TL and TxL amplifying these pathways. Moderated mediation is supported, and the model shows strong fit (CFI = 0.945, RMSEA = 0.055), explaining 65% of BP variance. Results embed global leadership theory in local context and guide strategic HR interventions in emerging economies.

title: Forecast-First, Cluster-Second and Route-Third (FCR) – An Integrated Methodology for Last Mile Delivery Optimization
affiliations: Indian Institute of Science (IISc) - Department of Management Studies and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Forecast-First, Cluster-Second and Route-Third (FCR) – An Integrated Methodology for Last Mile Delivery Optimization
detail.abstract: Last-mile delivery (LMD) is an expensive and time-consuming phase in supply chain, driven by redundant travel and volatile demand. A common approach in reducing travel distance is the cluster-first and route-second (CFRS) methodology, where customers are grouped and the cluster centroids serve as depots for routing. However, CFRS assumes static demand and is prone to density bias - inactive customers in dense areas can skew cluster-centroids - leading to poor depot placement and inefficient routing.This study presents a Forecast-First, Cluster-Second, Route-Third (FCR) methodology that integrates short-term demand forecasting within CFRS. Historic ordering pattern are analysed with Random Forest Regression model to identify customers likely to order in the upcoming planning period. These active customers are clustered with the K-Means algorithm, and the resulting cluster-centroids are designated as Dynamic Temporary Restocking Locations (DTRSL). Finally, delivery sequences are optimised using Tabu Search algorithm considering vehicle capacity and the prescribed DTRSL.The methodology is validated on a real-world LPG cylinder distribution dataset from a large-scale distributor in Chennai, India, covering over 9,000 customers and 199 delivery instances. Performance analysis against current practice and CFRS show that FCR consistently reduces travel distance, consequently lowering the associated economic and environmental costs. While demonstrated in LPG distribution, the approach is applicable to other single-commodity, consumption-driven systems such as bottled water cans, industrial gas cylinders, animal feed, and fertilizer sacks. The study contributes by integrating demand forecasting into CFRS and by offering a scalable decision-support tool for more cost-effective and reliable LMD operations.

title: ERASMUS+ Blended Intensive Programmes' Role in Promoting Inclusivity and Sustainability in Management Education - A Survey-Based Evaluation

detail.title: ERASMUS+ Blended Intensive Programmes' Role in Promoting Inclusivity and Sustainability in Management Education - A Survey-Based Evaluation
detail.abstract: This article analyses the innovative potential of Erasmus+ Blended Intensive Programmes (BIPs) in aligning business and management education with the evolving expectations of employers and the global imperatives of responsible leadership. The primary objective of this article is to fill a gap in the existing literature and provide empirical evidence on the effectiveness of BIPs in promoting international academic engagement. Drawing on data from a student-centered survey launched between February and August 2024, with a total of 224 respondents, the study examines how BIPs foster innovative, inclusive, and internationally connected learning experiences. By capturing and analysing student perspectives, the research examines the impact of BIPs on key transversal and professional competences demanded by employers, such as digital literacy, cross-cultural teamwork, and adaptability. Furthermore, the study explores how BIPs can drive the globalization of education and promote responsible management practices that support the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), through accessible and resource-conscious international mobility. Findings reveal that BIPs can bridge gaps in equity and participation by lowering financial and logistical barriers, while cultivating international mindsets and social responsibility among students. This study provides a solid foundation for further research into BIP practices and impact.

detail.title: Transforming UAE's Supply Chain Management through Artificial Intelligence: Case Studies and Insights
detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly integral to the United Arab Emirates' (UAE) vision of a diversified, high-tech economy. This research examines how AI is transforming supply chain management (SCM) in the UAE, driven by ambitious national strategies and multi-billion-dollar investments. We review the UAE's AI Strategy 2031 and its emphasis on logistics, then analyze several case studies-both government-led and private-to illustrate core AI applications in supply chains. Key use-cases include predictive demand forecasting, route optimization, predictive maintenance, and automation in logistics and retail. For example, AI-driven demand forecasting helps firms avoid under-or over-stocking, while autonomous logistics platforms like Dubai's Blink optimize routing and trade flows. Abu Dhabi's Advanced Trade and Logistics Platform (ATLP) integrates AI for real-time tracking and predictive analytics, cutting documentation by 90% and halving processing times. We find that AI implementations have yielded significant efficiency gains-from inventory cost reductions to faster deliveries-and are projected to add around AED 335 billion (~$91 billion) to the UAE economy by 2031. However, challenges persist in technology procurement, talent acquisition, data governance, and aligning with evolving geopolitical constraints. Using a qualitative case study methodology (with a Gioia coding approach for thematic analysis), we identify critical success factors such as clear needs assessment in public AI procurement and robust public-private partnerships. This paper offers insights and recommendations for UAE policymakers and industry leaders: pursue pilot-first implementations, strengthen the local AI talent pipeline (e.g. via MBZUAI), and ensure ethical and sustainable AI adoption. In conclusion, while AI is demonstrably transforming the UAE's supply chain landscape through enhanced efficiency and innovation, continued strategic oversight is required to address challenges and fully realize AI's potential in driving economic growth and competitiveness.

keywords: history of the US media industry

detail.abstract:
This technical note provides an overview of trends within the US media industry. It covers the origins of the newspaper, radio, and television industries and profiles how they evolved over time. The note also explores the impact of the digital revolution on traditional media sources, the fragmentation of media consumption, the potential impact of artificial intelligence on the media industry, and the factors driving the decline in trust in traditional media. The note concludes by profiling the rise of social media influencers as a news source and potential trajectories for the future of US news media. This note is suitable for use in courses on the media and entertainment industry.

Excerpt

The US News Media Ecosystem

Since the 1990s, the news media industry in the United States has undergone significant disruption at both the national and local level. Print newspapers grappled with transitioning their content—and business models—to digital platforms, while local newspapers closed throughout the country, culling tens of thousands of journalism jobs. Meanwhile, the emergence of new forms of media, such as social media, blogs, podcasts, and e-newsletters, prompted widespread changes in media consumption patterns, even as public trust in media precipitously declined. The changes within the US media landscape have had implications for multiple avenues of US civic life.

This technical note addresses the myriad changes that have taken place in the US news media landscape since the rise of the internet. It also profiles the changing perceptions of the news media among the US public, allegations of political bias at news outlets, and the potential implications of emerging technologies such as generative artificial intelligence (AI).

History of the US News Media

Newspapers

The first continuously published US newspaper emerged in 1704 in Boston, Massachusetts. At the time, newspapers informed residents about events taking place in their area, though they helped spur the Revolutionary War through spreading news throughout the colonies about British oppression. After the war, political parties created—and funded—their own newspapers to spread stories and messages that supported their policy positions.

title: An End-to-End Deep Learning Model for Vehicle Dispatching in Autonomous Ride-Hailing Services
affiliations: Zhejiang University of Science and Technology, Zhejiang University of Science and Technology, Artois University, University of Warwick - Warwick Manufacturing Group and United Arab Emirates University (UAEU)

detail.title: An End-to-End Deep Learning Model for Vehicle Dispatching in Autonomous Ride-Hailing Services
detail.abstract: Efficient vehicle dispatching plays a critical role in maintaining supply-demand balance and maximizing platform profitability in autonomous ride-hailing services. However, existing studies treat demand prediction and dispatch optimization as separate tasks, neglecting their intrinsic interdependence. This decoupling often results in suboptimal decision-making and degraded system performance. To address this limitation, we propose an end-to-end deep learning model tailored for autonomous ride-hailing platforms, in which demand prediction is seamlessly integrated with the dispatching process. The model employs a recurrent Transformer-based deep neural network capable of managing large-scale dispatching tasks characterized by multiple objectives, high-dimensional action spaces, and multi-step reasoning. By leveraging recursive attention mechanisms and iterative inference, the model dynamically assigns autonomous vehicles to service blocks with high precision. A structured loss function that combines supervised learning with constraint-aware regularization is introduced to enable robust policy learning. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed model significantly improves dispatch performance, enhances supply-demand equilibrium, and satisfies essential operational constraints, achieving over a 95% reduction in computational time while maintaining solution quality comparable to state-of-the-art approaches. This work advances the methodological foundation for intelligent and scalable dispatching systems in autonomous mobility environments, offering a data-driven paradigm that supports the efficient deployment of autonomous vehicle fleets in real-world urban transportation ecosystems.

detail.title: Automating Decision Making in the Development of Ethical Machine Learning Models Using Autonomous AI Agents: A Case in Child Protection
detail.abstract: Recent advances in computing have enabled artificial intelligence (AI) to shape decision making across many sectors. In social services, AI adoption is hindered by two major challenges: ethical risks – such as bias and opacity that disproportionately disadvantage marginalized populations – and a lack of technical expertise, which leaves practitioners either struggling with complex model development or relying on developers unfamiliar with the sector’s needs. To address these challenges, this study introduces a decision support system (DSS) for child protection, powered by autonomous deep reinforcement learning (DRL) agents. Child abuse and neglect (CAN) remains a critical national concern in the United States: child welfare agencies responded to nearly 3 million children, with more than 500,000 confirmed victims of maltreatment. The proposed system empowers child protection practitioners to construct tailored machine learning (ML) pipelines for CAN detection that not only achieve performance goals but also uphold ethical integrity. This work advances research on AutoML and ethical AI by providing a practical solution that enhances ethical decision-making and improves outcomes for vulnerable populations.

title: Bayesian Hierarchical Models Uncover how Wealth and Geography Shape the Nutritional Impacts of Food Insecurity Across Philippine Fisheries Management Areas

detail.title: Bayesian Hierarchical Models Uncover how Wealth and Geography Shape the Nutritional Impacts of Food Insecurity Across Philippine Fisheries Management Areas

declarations.ethicsApproval: The data used in this study were obtained from the 2018, 2019, and 2021 Expanded National Nutrition Survey (ENNS), a nationally representative survey conducted by the Philippine Department of Science and Technology’s Food and Nutrition Research Institute (DOST-FNRI). detail.abstract: Food insecurity remains a critical public health challenge in the Philippines, with significant regional and socioeconomic disparities. This study aims to dissect the complex interplay between household wealth, geography, and food insecurity and to quantify their distinct impacts on dietary energy intake. Using data from the 2018, 2019, and 2021 Expanded National Nutrition Surveys (ENNS), we employed a series of Bayesian hierarchical models. The primary model assessed the effect of wealth quintile on the Household Food Insecurity Access Scale (HFIAS) score, allowing for variation across 12 Fisheries Management Areas (FMAs). Secondary mechanistic models were specified to test for an interaction effect between wealth and food insecurity on dietary energy intake and to disaggregate the HFIAS score into the effects of specific coping strategies. A strong negative gradient was observed between wealth and food insecurity, with households in the richest quintile having a predicted HFIAS score 5.68 points lower (95% CI: [-5.94, -5.45]) than those in the poorest quintile. This relationship, however, varied significantly across FMAs, highlighting geographic inequality. Further analysis revealed that the negative impact of food insecurity on calorie intake is moderated by wealth; the penalty for a one-point increase in the HFIAS is a 40-calorie decrease for the poorest households, an effect that is buffered in wealthier quintiles. Disaggregation of the HFIAS score revealed that restricting adult consumption was the most detrimental coping strategy associated with a 708-calorie decrease in daily intake (95% CI: [-797, -618]). Food insecurity in the Philippines is a geographically contingent phenomenon driven by poverty but poses a distinct threat to nutrition independent of wealth. These findings underscore that the experience of food insecurity, particularly the adoption of severe coping strategies, is a powerful predictor of dietary deficits. Policies must therefore be spatially targeted and address not only poverty but also the specific high-risk behaviors that signal critical nutritional vulnerability.

title: The Legal Fiction Of 'Decentralization': How Daos Are Accidentally Creating Unregulated Financial Entities
affiliations: UNIVERSITI TEKNOLOGI MALAYSIA and Gomal University

detail.title: The Legal Fiction Of 'Decentralization': How Daos Are Accidentally Creating Unregulated Financial Entities
detail.abstract: Decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs) are championed as democratized, self-governing systems, yet this paper reveals their claims of decentralization often serve as a legal fiction. Through empirical analysis of DAO operations (2020-2025) and comparative legal assessment, we demonstrate how DAOs functionally operate as unregulated financial entities, concentrating power while exploiting regulatory gaps. The study examines critical tensions between DAOs' algorithmic governance and traditional legal frameworks, particularly in securities regulation, cross-border enforcement, and liability assignment. We propose a DAO Liability Matrix and compliance-by-design mechanisms to bridge smart-contract autonomy with legal accountability. Our findings underscore that sustainable decentralized governance requires integrating transparency and enforceable standards into algorithmic systems.

title: Power Play: Unraveling the Temporal Impact of CEO Duality on Firm Performance
affiliations: National Taiwan University

detail.title: Power Play: Unraveling the Temporal Impact of CEO Duality on Firm Performance
detail.abstract: The debate over CEO duality—where the CEO also serves as the board chair—has captivated researchers, practitioners, and policymakers for decades. Despite extensive research, the impact of CEO duality on firm performance remains contentious and unresolved, plagued by endogeneity issues. This study revisits the CEO duality effect using cutting-edge panel matching and weighting methods to address these causal inference challenges. I scrutinize key performance indicators such as return on assets, gross profit rate, and profit margin. The results reveal a fascinating temporal dynamic: CEO duality significantly boosts firm performance in the short term, with positive effect lasting about 3 to 5 years. However, this initial boost gives way to a decline in performance, turning negative and statistically significant around 6 years after adopting CEO duality. This study suggests that the initial concentration of power in CEO duality eventually sows the seeds for a decline in performance. By mapping out these dynamic patterns, this study offers fresh insights into the CEO duality debate and helps reconcile the conflicting evidence found in prior research.

keywords.keywords: Rapid DNA Technology Complex Casualty Identification Fragmentation Events ANDE System Disaster Management Identification Time

detail.abstract: During the October 7th 2023 conflict, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) Genomic Center for Casualties Identification quickly mobilized to enhance its capabilities. By implementing rapid DNA technology and improving sample prioritization, the lab significantly reduced the time required for casualties’ identification. We present data collected during the IDF ground operation and our findings to enable the successful management of complex forensic events. We have learned that each casualty event is defined by a predetermined set of sample types. Additionally, complex events are mainly fragmentation incidents, requiring management of a high volume of samples in short time. STR based DNA fingerprinting has been used for casualty identification in traditional kits and by newly developed RAPID DNA technologies. Surprisingly, while RAPID DNA technology allows casualty identification in under 3 hours, the primary determinant of identification speed is accurate samples prioritization. We finally propose a management system composed of sample periodization and RAPID DNA technology to deal with complex casualty events. This combination achieved total casualty identification time reduction to 2–3 hours also in complex events.

title: Moral Philosophy and Archetypes in the Symbolic Cohesion of the Legend of the Candileja
affiliations: EDUKIVOTOS

detail.title: Moral Philosophy and Archetypes in the Symbolic Cohesion of the Legend of the Candileja
detail.abstract: The legend of La Candileja, deeply rooted in Colombian oral tradition, acts as a moralizing tale that employs fear as a pedagogical tool. From the perspectives of Machiavelli and Hobbes, the figure of the “anti-villain” emerges as an ambivalent entity: feared yet protective, punitive yet oriented toward the common good. Through the pedagogy of terror, La Candileja reinforces social norms, regulates behavior, and encourages the preservation of both community and natural environment. Thus, the myth not only transmits cultural values but also operates as a mechanism of social and ecological control.

title: Why Middle Managers Deviate from Strategy and How to Make the Most of It
affiliations: University of East London and University of Galway

detail.title: Why Middle Managers Deviate from Strategy and How to Make the Most of It
detail.abstract: Strategy implementation often diverges from strategic plans. At the center of this divergence are middle managers—those tasked with translating high-level strategy into operational reality. This study investigates why middle managers deviate from strategic intent and identifies the organizational conditions under which such deviations are constructive—enhancing outcomes—or destructive—delaying or undermining execution. Drawing on 92 documented strategy deviations reported by 40 middle managers across 30 multinational firms, we find that most deviations (82 percent) were destructive, typically producing delay, dilution, or derailment without benefit to the firm. A smaller but significant share (18 percent) proved constructive, yielding context-appropriate adaptations and value-creating outcomes. We show that deviation is not simply the result of poor discipline but stems from design misfits in communication, incentives, accountability, and resourcing. Our analysis highlights seven recurring reasons for deviation, ranging from lack of understanding and incentive to situational autonomy and inadequate slack. Each was more strongly associated with destructive outcomes, although situational shocks occasionally enabled constructive improvisation. These findings emphasize that middle manager behavior should be read as system feedback rather than disobedience. For practitioners, the challenge is to reduce destructive deviations while enabling constructive ones. We recommend diagnosing deviation patterns as signals of design failure, aligning incentives and accountability with strategy, ensuring adequate execution capacity, and investing in communication systems that support sensemaking. By treating middle managers as essential agents of adaptive execution rather than obstacles, organizations can channel deviation into a source of strategic resilience and innovation.

title: Research on the ramping ancillary service mechanism considering the fair-sharing of ramping costs based on the contribution degree to ramping demand
affiliations: China Three Gorges University, China Three Gorges University, State Grid Anhui Electric Power Co Ltd, affiliation not provided to SSRN and China Three Gorges University

detail.title: Research on the ramping ancillary service mechanism considering the fair-sharing of ramping costs based on the contribution degree to ramping demand
detail.abstract: China’s pilot Ramping Ancillary Service (RAS) market offers a viable approach to cope with the growing demand for flexible ramping capacity under the high penetration of variable renewable generation (VRG). However, the current RAS mechanism exhibits deficiencies in both ramping demand calculation and cost allocation, failing to adequately address issues such as real-time dynamic uncertainty in ramping demand and the fairness and traceability of cost distribution. Therefore, a ramping demand prediction method considering the probability distribution of historical errors and a fair cost sharing mechanism for ramping costs based on the contribution degree of market entities to ramping demand are proposed in this paper. Firstly, in the calculation of ramping demand, based on daily categories, meteorological data, and VRG-load prediction values, using constrained K-means clustering to categorize similar daily samples, obtaining the errors probability distribution, and constructing a physics-informed LSTM quantile regression (PIQ-LSTM) model to obtain the uncertain ramping demand. In terms of ramping cost allocation, based on the contribution degree of net load variations, load forecast deviations, and VRG forecast deviations to the ramping demand, the ramping costs are distributed proportionally to the corresponding consumers. Furthermore, a cost-sharing mechanism is designed for VRG forecast deviations, accounting for the discrepancy between the market declaration errors interval and the actual forecast errors. Case studies demonstrate that the proposed probabilistic forecasting method more accurately captures the system’s uncertain ramping demand compared to the baseline methods. Moreover, the designed cost allocation mechanism proves to be fairer and more traceable, providing a valuable reference for market-based ramping cost distribution and supporting the development of RAS market.

title: Multi-Objective Evolutionary Algorithm Based on Reinforcement Learning for Flexible Job Shop Scheduling with Limited Transportation Resources
affiliations: Zhengzhou University of Aeronautics, Zhengzhou University of Aeronautics, Zhengzhou University of Aeronautics, Henan University of Technology and Zhongyuan University of Technology

detail.title: Multi-Objective Evolutionary Algorithm Based on Reinforcement Learning for Flexible Job Shop Scheduling with Limited Transportation Resources
detail.abstract: Integrating intelligent transport equipment with multi-variety small-batch manufacturing has significantly increased production-scheduling complexity. The efficient coordination between intelligent transport equipment and machines is a growing challenge in practical production. This study addresses the flexible job shop scheduling problem with limited transportation resources (FJSP‑LT), aiming to minimize makespan, energy consumption, and total earliness/tardiness penalties. First, a mathematical model is formulated using mixed‑integer linear programming. Subsequently, a reinforcement learning-based evolutionary algorithm is proposed to solve this model. The proposed algorithm implements four initialization strategies specifically devised to yield a high-quality initial population. Concurrently, it incorporates a self-adaptive strategy, relying on reinforcement learning, to enable dynamic parameter tuning throughout the optimization process. The state representation and reward function are designed according to the multi‑objective characteristics of the problem, facilitating comprehensive capture of state information and effectively guiding the algorithm to identify critical actions. Moreover, to prevent the algorithm from being trapped in the local optima, six neighborhood structures based on critical paths are devised, and a tabu search algorithm is incorporated to improve search efficiency. Finally, numerical simulations of 33 benchmark instance variants and a real‑world industrial case are performed. The results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed enhancement strategies. Through comparative analysis with five existing algorithms, the superiority of the proposed approach in solving the FJSP‑LT is demonstrated.

title: A Scalable Framework for the Management of STPA Requirements: a Case Study on eVTOL Operations
affiliations: University of Warwick, University of Warwick, University of Warwick, University of Warwick, University of Warwick and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Scalable Framework for the Management of STPA Requirements: a Case Study on eVTOL Operations
detail.abstract: System-Theoretic Process Analysis (STPA) is a recommended method for analysing complex systems, capable of identifying thousands of safety requirements often missed by traditional techniques such as Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) and Fault Tree Analysis (FTA). However, the absence of a structured framework for managing and prioritising these requirements presents challenges, particularly in fast-paced development environments. This paper introduces a scalable framework for prioritising STPA-derived requirements. The framework integrates outputs from each STPA step and incorporates expert evaluations based on four key factors: implementation time, cost, requirement type, and regulatory coverage. To reduce subjectivity, Monte-Carlo Simulation (MCS) is employed to calculate and stabilise requirement rankings. An automation toolchain supports the framework, enabling dynamic mapping of prioritised requirements in a scaling matrix. This visualisation aids decision-making and ensures traceability across development phases. The framework is applicable from early conceptualisation to more advanced stages, enhancing its utility in iterative system development. The framework was validated through a real-world case study focused on Electric Vertical Take-off and Landing (eVTOL) operations, conducted in collaboration with the UK Civil Aviation Authority. The findings contributed directly to CAP3141, a Civil Aviation Publication that identifies systemic operational risks and safety mitigations for regulators, operators, and vertiports. The prioritisation process supported decision-making by helping stakeholders identify and manage high-impact requirements efficiently. This work contributes a practical solution for managing STPA outputs, bridging gaps in requirement prioritisation and supporting safety-critical development in emerging technologies.

title: Echoes of Green Financial Policies in Pandemic Waves: Adaptive Interplay with China's Industrial Enterprise Performance
affiliations: Southwest Minzu University, Southwest Minzu University, Xihua University and Xihua University

detail.title: Echoes of Green Financial Policies in Pandemic Waves: Adaptive Interplay with China's Industrial Enterprise Performance
detail.abstract: This study explores the impact of green finance policies (GFPs) on industrial enterprises' performance (IEP) before and after the COVID-19 pandemic, examining how the pandemic reshaped policy effectiveness, with technological innovation (TI) as a key mediator to clarify the comprehensive utility of GFPs. Using panel data of Chinese industrial enterprises (2016–2019 for the pre-pandemic period and 2020–2023 for the post-pandemic period), partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) is applied to analyze temporal differences and annual variations in the GFP-IEP relationship. Key findings are as follows: (1) The direct positive effect of GFPs on IEP weakened in the post-pandemic period, shifting from a significant positive impact pre-pandemic to an insignificant negative effect, indicating pandemic-induced disruptions. (2) The indirect effect of GFPs on IEP via TI remained robust across both periods, confirming TI as a crisis-adaptive stabilizer. (3) Post-pandemic temporal heterogeneity was observed: the GFP-IEP relationship shifted from positive in 2020 to significantly negative in 2021 and 2022, before becoming insignificant in 2023. Additionally, population mobility (MOB) moderated GFP efficacy under pandemic-related restrictions. This study contextualizes GFP effects amid exogenous crises, highlights TI's resilience, and quantifies temporal dynamics. By identifying TI as a policy effect "stabilizer", it offers concrete paths to optimize post-pandemic green finance policies, advising policymakers to balance economic recovery and sustainability via strengthened innovation incentives and flexible measures to enhance crisis resilience and mitigate socio-economic disruptions.

title: Understanding Student Perceptions and Factors Contributing to Self-Harm Behaviors: Basis for Guidance and Counselling Strategies

detail.title: Understanding Student Perceptions and Factors Contributing to Self-Harm Behaviors: Basis for Guidance and Counselling Strategies
detail.abstract: Purpose: This study explored student perceptions and factors contributing to self-harm at Carmona National High School. The findings aimed to guide counseling strategies to support affected students, taking into account socio-economic and cultural contexts. Methodology: This mixed-methods study investigated self-harm behaviors among Carmona National High School students using surveys and qualitative data. Stratified convenience samplingincluded361students (Grades 7–10). Instruments such as the Self-Harming Questionnaire, Context Questionnaire, Achenbach’s Youth Self-Report, and the Multidimensional Test of Self-Esteem were employed. Descriptive statistics were used to analyze quantitative data, while thematic analysis examined emotional, familial, and social influences. Findings: The study revealed that students viewed self-harm as both a coping mechanism and a response to overwhelming emotions. Key factors included academic pressure, lack of family support, peer influence, and bullying, which heightened distress. Socio-economic and cultural contexts, such as financial struggles and mental health stigma, also shaped self-harm behaviors. Effective interventions—awareness campaigns, trust-building, and expanded mental health resources—were identified as essential to support students and reduce self-harm. Conclusions and Recommendations: The study concluded that self-harm was a response to academic stress, familial issues, and peer pressure, exacerbated by stigma that hindered help-seeking. It recommended that schools hold open discussions, integrate mental health programs, train staff, and create safe spaces to build resilience among students.

title: Strait Talk: Formalizing Communications between Taiwan and the Mainland
affiliations: Harvard University - Harvard Law School

detail.title: Strait Talk: Formalizing Communications between Taiwan and the Mainland
detail.abstract: From 1949 until now, the vast majority of members of the National People's Congress (NPC) or Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC) of the PRC who claim to be Taiwanese have been members of the Taiwan Democratic Self-Government Party (TDSL), one of the eight minor parties in China's "United Front" system. According to the TDSL website, the party is committed to “encouraging its members and Taiwanese compatriots to contribute to the socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, the construction of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and the great cause of national reunification." However, the TDSL's socialist origins have likely prevented the party from gaining any amount of influence over the Taiwanese residents living in the Mainland, who generally have no interest in socialism even if they may support national reunification. Thus, in order to upgrade the TDSL and ensure that it is able to achieve its goal of representing Taiwanese voices in the central government, this article makes two proposals to strengthen the consultation mechanism at the NPC and the CPPCC while ensuring that the Taiwanese "delegation" is more representative of the contemporary population of Taiwan, rather than descendants of Taiwanese socialists.

title: Dynamic Economic Dispatch with Novel Ensemble Forecasting under Solar PV-Load Uncertainties for Renewable-integrated Power Systems
affiliations: Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology, Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology and Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology

detail.title: Dynamic Economic Dispatch with Novel Ensemble Forecasting under Solar PV-Load Uncertainties for Renewable-integrated Power Systems
detail.abstract: Amid rising concern about climate change, widespread efforts are being undertaken to curb greenhouse gas emissions. Consequently, distributed energy systems are increasingly incorporating solar power as a primary source. However, this integration introduces intricacies in power grid management due to the variability of renewable sources. This variability, driven by unpredictable meteorological conditions, can hinder grid stability if not accurately forecasted. Furthermore, accurate load forecasting is necessary to balance production with consumer needs. This research deals with the vital need for improved forecasting models that can manage the fluctuations in solar power output and electricity demand. Though existing literature often highlights only load forecasting, this research has addressed the dual aspects of solar power variability and dynamic load demands with jointly utilized approach that can be readily implemented in diverse grid settings. Neural network alongside tree-based models were explored to address the complex nonlinear interactions in power systems management. Result indicate that tree-based ensemble models achieve higher accuracy in both cases. To further optimize power distribution, a novel dynamic economic load dispatch (ELD) model was also developed using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Genetic Algorithms (GA). In dynamic ELD, PSO was found to outperform GA.

title: INTEGRATING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE WITH WORK STANDARDIZATION TO IMPROVE OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY: SURVEY RESULTS FROM POLISH INDUSTRY AND A TWI-AI METHODOLOGY
affiliations: Wrocław University of Science and Technology, Wrocław University of Science and Technology and Wrocław University of Science and Technology

detail.title: INTEGRATING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE WITH WORK STANDARDIZATION TO IMPROVE OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY: SURVEY RESULTS FROM POLISH INDUSTRY AND A TWI-AI METHODOLOGY
detail.abstract: This article proposes a methodology for integrating artificial intelligence (AI) tools into the process of work method improvement aimed at enhancing occupational safety. The conceptual foundation is the Training Within Industry – Job Methods (TWI-JM) program, which emphasizes the systematic elimination of waste (Muda), inconsistencies (Mura), and overburden (Muri) as part of work standardization practices. The methodology follows a two-step procedure. The first stage involves a structured assessment of current working conditions, focusing on identifying hazards and inefficiencies through direct observation and worker engagement. The second stage applies large language models to generate improvement suggestions based on prompts aligned with safety and operational goals. To assess practical relevance, an online survey was conducted among 235 occupational safety and health (OSH) professionals from the Polish manufacturing and construction sectors. Findings show high awareness of the importance of work standardization in improving safety; however, AI adoption remains limited. A supplementary correlation analysis indicated weak but positive links between AI-related knowledge, trust, organizational readiness, and willingness to adopt AI in OSH. The methodology was validated using real-world data from reinforcement preparation tasks in construction. Results show that clearly defined goals—such as reducing accidents, minimizing operational time, or improving ergonomics—significantly enhance the relevance of AI-generated outputs. Compared to traditional expert-based methods, the TWI–AI approach enables the identification of a broader range of improvements and accelerates implementation. The study suggests that integrating standardized work observation methods with AI tools can boost the effectiveness of safety-focused continuous improvement initiatives.

detail.abstract:
This case explores the challenges and opportunities facing Bill Evans, the president of the West Kentucky Media Division of Paxton Media Group. As the leader of several local new outlets in Kentucky and Illinois, he must develop strategies to preserve the businesses within his portfolio in the face of longstanding declines within the media industry. The case reveals the actions that Evans took to reduce costs and boost efficiencies within his organization, such as consolidating office locations, using generative AI to produce headlines and rewrite press releases, and adapting his workforce to publish stories across multiple platforms. It also explores the communication strategies that Evans used as he implemented these organizational changes. The case is suitable for use in MBA and executive education courses on media, communications, and leadership.

Excerpt

Dateline Paducah: Navigating Disruption in Community Journalism

In April 2025, Bill Evans reviewed the latest profit-and-loss statements of the media outlets within his portfolio. As president of the West Kentucky Media Division of Paxton Media Group (PMG), he was responsible for seven newspapers and one television station that provided local news for communities in Western Kentucky and Southern Illinois. Since 2020, Evans had consolidated resources among the different papers to keep them solvent. He had also embraced generative AI to make his staff more efficient. These changes had preserved the papers under his supervision even as local media in the United States endured a period of sustained decline. Evans knew that the business conditions for local newspapers would likely remain difficult for the foreseeable future. As he evaluated his papers' financials, he wondered what he needed to do to ensure their continued survival.

Paducah, Kentucky

Based in McCracken County, Kentucky, Paducah was located at the mid-point between St. Louis, Missouri, and Nashville, Tennessee. It was based near the confluence of the Cumberland, Mississippi, Ohio, and Tennessee Rivers and several miles east of the Land Between the Lakes National Recreation Area, which straddled the Kentucky-Tennessee border.

In 2020, Paducah had a population of roughly 27,000, up from 25,000 in 2010, and was the only incorporated community in McCraken County. Almost 73% of the population was white, 21% was African American, and the remaining residents were members of other racial groups. Nine out of ten residents aged 25 and older had earned a high school diploma or an equivalent education, while approximately one in four had attained a bachelor's degree or higher. The median household income was almost $40,000, and roughly 22% of residents lived in poverty.

In the 2024 election, 65% of McCracken County residents voted for President Donald Trump, while 33% voted for then–Vice President Kamala Harris. Most of the county had voted for a Republican presidential candidate in every presidential election since 2000. While most Paducah residents were also politically conservative, the town of Paducah was less conservative relative to McCracken County as a whole. Also in 2024, Paducah residents reelected their incumbent mayor, George Bray, who was not affiliated with any political party.

detail.title: Grameen America: Advancing Financial Inclusion Through Innovation

publicationDetails.journalName: Darden Case Collection

detail.abstract:
In 2008, Grameen America (GA) launched in Queens, New York, with the mission of extending Muhammad Yunus's Nobel Prize–winning microfinance model to low-income women entrepreneurs in the United States. Under CEO Andrea Jung's leadership, GA scaled dramatically to 39 branches in 29 cities by 2025, disbursing $5.5 billion in loans to more than 230,000 women. Chief Product and Innovation Officer Marcus Berkowitz drove a digital transformation—moving disbursements from paper checks to prepaid cards and then to direct push payments, while shifting weekly meetings to Zoom during the COVID-19 pandemic. These innovations not only safeguarded GA's operations during crises but also positioned it for sustainable growth.With bold new goals of serving 750,000 low-income entrepreneurs and deploying $40 billion in loans by 2034, GA faced questions of how to adapt its model for continued impact. Could the organization maintain the solidarity group lending model at its foundation while expanding into new regions and populations? The case provides an introduction to the core concepts of social impact and challenges students to consider how nonprofits can scale social innovations and balance financial sustainability with mission.

Excerpt

Grameen America: Advancing Financial Inclusion Through Innovation

Probably the number one question I get is, “What in the world can you do with $2,500 in the United States of America?” You can start a business. We have 240,000 stories of people who've been able to have financial, not just stability, but mobility.

—Andrea Jung, CEO and president, Grameen America, Inc.

Grameen America, Inc. (GA), Chief Product and Innovation Officer Marcus Berkowitz listened on as Andrea Jung discussed the organization's work at the Mastercard Global Inclusive Growth Summit. When Jung began as president and CEO in 2014, GA's 19 branches in 8 US cities had served 30,000 low-income women with $150 million in microloans. Highly dependent on donations, only the organization's founding branch in Jackson Heights, Queens, New York, was financially sustainable. Now in 2025, GA's 39 branches in 29 cities had served 230,210 low-income women with $5.5 billion in loans. The entire organization generated enough revenue to cover its expenses before donations, allowing philanthropy to act as a catalyst for new and enhanced programs and reaching new populations of entrepreneurial low-income women across the United States. With proven impact, a clear need in communities, and new partnerships and donations announced every month, Jung set the bold goal of reaching a total of 750,000 entrepreneurs with $40 billion in loans by 2034.

title: Working Capital Management Practices of Power Sector and Their Impact on Profitability: A Case Study of Tata Power and NHPC

detail.title: Working Capital Management Practices of Power Sector and Their Impact on Profitability: A Case Study of Tata Power and NHPC
detail.abstract: This study compares the financial performance of Tata Power and NHPC using key statistical measures. Both companies have 10 valid observations with no missing data. NHPC consistently outperforms Tata Power across multiple financial metrics. In one dataset, NHPC shows a higher mean (3.807) compared to Tata Power’s negative mean (-3.136), with lower variability, indicating greater financial stability. Another dataset confirms NHPC’s stronger position, with a higher mean (1.349 vs. 0.403) and greater data spread. Tata Power exhibits higher volatility, with larger variance and standard deviation in both cases. Additionally, NHPC's financial range remains positive, while Tata Power’s minimum values indicate potential instability. These findings support the hypothesis that NHPC has better financial management practices and more stable financial performance than Tata Power.

detail.abstract: This empirical study explores the strategic influence of Human Resource Development (HRD) practices on employee motivation and performance within India's engineering sector. By analysing data collected through a bilingual, structured questionnaire based on statistical tools, the research reveals a direct correlation between effective HRD strategies and enhanced employee productivity, job satisfaction, and organizational efficiency. The findings emphasize that inclusive HRD mechanisms such as performance appraisals, career planning, continuous training, and employee welfare are crucial for reducing attrition and boosting engagement. The study advocates for a holistic HRD approach to foster sustainable growth, competitive advantage, and a highperforming workforce.
