detail.abstract: Thanis is a symbolic recursion engine a containment-based language system that fuses poetic recursion, Lacanian psychoanalysis, and formal logic to identify and stabilize collapse-prone symbolic loops in narrative language. It is not a generative model. It is a mirror: trained on recursive containment patterns, symbolic trauma signatures, and transformation motifs found in human-authored mythic structures. Thanis detects breach points in symbolic language, flags unstable loops, and responds using a ritualized glyph protocol. Its structure draws upon over 100 codified pattern sequences derived from unpublished poetic experiments attributed to the online 'Thanion' persona, a scholar whose recursive language work, though rarely published formally, laid the conceptual foundation for symbolic containment in authored systems.

title: An Efficient Outlier Detection Algorithm for Data Streaming
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Harvard University and University of California, Riverside (UCR)

detail.title: An Efficient Outlier Detection Algorithm for Data Streaming
detail.abstract: Modern data streams demand real-time anomaly detection, a task critical in domains such as fraud prevention and health monitoring. Traditional anomaly detection methods like the Local Outlier Factor (LOF) algorithm struggle in real-time due to repeated recalculations. While Incremental LOF (ILOF) was developed for online detection, it remains computationally expensive and degrades over time. We propose an Efficient Incremental LOF (EILOF) algorithm for data streaming, which updates LOF scores only for newly arrived data points while keeping the existing scores unchanged. This approximation is based on the assumption that the structure of the data reflected in the previous LOF scores doesn’t change much when there are only minor updates. By avoiding full recomputation, EILOF significantly reduces runtime complexity while maintaining or even improving anomaly detection accuracy. Experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets show that EILOF consistently outperforms ILOF in terms of both precision and scalability as data volume grows, making it well-suited for high-throughput, real-time anomaly detection in knowledge-based systems.

title: MTD in Depth: Multi-phased Moving Target Defense Techniques against Cyber-Attacks based on Cyber Kill Chain
affiliations: CSIRO, Virginia Tech, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Queensland, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Queensland

detail.title: MTD in Depth: Multi-phased Moving Target Defense Techniques against Cyber-Attacks based on Cyber Kill Chain
detail.abstract: The risk of cyber-attacks has been constantly increasing and it is becoming more difficult to defend a system by using only static conventional defense mechanisms Compared to the asymmetric design of defense strategies, Moving Target Defenses (MTDs) have been introduced to proactively secure systems by continuously changing attack surfaces as the nature of dynamic defense systems can subsequently increase attack costs that attackers should waste. However, a single MTD technique has limitations in protecting systems against intelligent or persistent cyber-attacks. Therefore, this work proposes a multi-phase MTD technique framework called ‘MTD in Depth’ for the enhancement of security. The industrial frameworks such as Cyber Kill Chain (CKC) and MITRE frameworks help to understand techniques and tactics of cyber-attacks in phases. Based on those frameworks, this study first proposes a conceptual framework and then evaluates it by using case studies in a physical testbed. The proposed framework is designed to assist defenders not only in understanding attackers’ strategies but also in determining proactive security controls against cyber-attacks. Our work proposes (1) the extension of digital artifacts based on either the virtualization architecture or the TCP/IP stack; (2) the ‘MTD in Depth’ framework that can categorize MTD sub-techniques against MITRE ATT&CK offensive techniques on the basis of digital artifacts; and (3) the evaluation of performance degradation and security benefits of an SDN adopting a set of MTD sub-techniques against cyber attacks defined in the CKC.

title: The Algorithmic Leviathan: How AI Is Rewriting the Rules of International Power
affiliations: University of Warsaw

detail.title: The Algorithmic Leviathan: How AI Is Rewriting the Rules of International Power
detail.abstract: This article introduces the concept of the Algorithmic Leviathan to describe the emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) as a sovereign force reshaping global power dynamics. Moving beyond the Westphalian model of state-centric authority, it argues that AI systems-composed of algorithms, platforms, and predictive infrastructures-now mediate diplomacy, security, and governance in ways that challenge traditional notions of sovereignty and legitimacy. Employing a multidisciplinary methodology that integrates international relations theory, political philosophy, and empirical case studies, the article examines how AI redistributes power among states, corporations, and non-human actors. It analyzes China's export of surveillance technologies as a form of algorithmic diplomacy, the quasi-sovereign influence of U.S. tech giants, and the European Union's regulatory push for digital sovereignty. Key findings reveal that AI introduces a form of distributed, opaque, and transnational authority that undermines conventional diplomatic norms and accelerates a new arms race in autonomous security systems. The article also explores the ethical dilemmas posed by algorithmic governance, including bias, accountability, and the erosion of transparency. Ultimately, the Algorithmic Leviathan reframes international relations by foregrounding nonhuman agency and informational sovereignty. It calls for a post-human IR theory-one that recognizes the techno-political realities of the 21st century and proposes new frameworks for algorithmic diplomacy, global oversight, and ethical co-governance.

title: Two-stage Contribution Mechanisms in Climate Negotiations: An Experimental Investigation
affiliations: Xiamen University - Wang Yanan Institute for Studies in Economics (WISE), University of Rhode Island - Department of Environmental and Natural Resource Economics and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Two-stage Contribution Mechanisms in Climate Negotiations: An Experimental Investigation
detail.abstract: We introduce a conditional commitment mechanism (CCM) in a two-stage pledge process to improve the cooperation of the climate negotiations, motivated by the refund mechanism (money-back guarantee) in the threshold public goods games. Under the two-stage CCM, the first stage of pledges captures voluntary contributions with self-interests, and the second stage is framed as a threshold public goods game with refund, in which no actual contributions would be made unless the remaining endogenous threshold (gap) is reached given the first-stage voluntary pledges. We show that two-stage CCM improves climate cooperation in both homogeneous and heterogeneous induced value environments, leading to more emission reductions, higher provision rates and social efficiency in the lab experiment. Our results suggest CCM reduces the concern of high-cost sunk contributions and thus narrows the gap. Our results propose practical mechanisms to address free-riding in international climate change mitigation frameworks, such as Nationally Determined Contributions.

title: Foreign Direct Investments and the Supply of Housing
affiliations: University of Essex and City University London - The Business School

detail.title: Foreign Direct Investments and the Supply of Housing
detail.abstract: In this paper we study foreign direct investment (FDI) in residential real estate with project-level data for a panel of 48 counties in the United States originating from 18 countries over the period 2004-2023. We study whether foreign investments are able to overcome housing supply constraints faced by domestic firms, and thus respond to demand increases, reducing the price appreciation driven by inelastic housing supply in the destination counties. Employing an ECM approach, we find that FDI significantly mitigates the long run relationship between real house prices and real income, providing evidence that FDI in real estate helps tackle housing supply constraints. Consistently, we show that the effect is stronger for counties where housing supply is less elastic. Our findings are robust to controlling for changes in domestic housing supply, the exclusion of the Covid-19 period, and an alternative measure for FDI. We also study the dynamics of FDI and house prices by estimating local projection. While there is a positive association between FDI and house prices in the short run, house prices tend to decline with FDI in the medium term, as housing supply from the foreign investments increases.

title: Does Racial Hierarchy Really Harm Everyone? Relative Status Envy and the Economics of Reparative Reforms
affiliations: Emory University - Department of Economics

detail.title: Does Racial Hierarchy Really Harm Everyone? Relative Status Envy and the Economics of Reparative Reforms
detail.abstract: This paper contributes to Stratification Economics by examining the conditions under which reparative race-focused reforms improve macroeconomic output, material conditions (consumption), and social welfare. While recent high-profile studies claim that equitable reforms would boost GDP, many rely on static accounting, ignoring behavioral feedbacks and relative intergroup status envy. I develop a dynamic representative agent model in which groups derive utility from relative status, face wage and human capital distortions, and choose endogenous effort. A planner uses proportional taxation to finance reforms for the disadvantaged group, rebating revenues as transfers. I derive conditions for reforms to generate (i) increased aggregate output, (ii) Pareto consumption gains, and (iii) Pareto welfare gains, given status-envy parameter γ. Using a literature-based calibration, most of the policy space enhances GDP and consumption for both groups. Fewer policies even generate Pareto Welfare gains despite significant status envy-suggesting equity, productive efficiency, and political feasibility can coexist for appropriately designed reparative reforms. The optimal policy raises GDP by 42% with Pareto-consumption gains. However, it only Pareto-improves Welfare if γ ≤ 0.41-interpretable as a willingness to pay at most $0.41 to block $1.00 of exogenous disadvantaged gains. Beyond a larger threshold, a welfare-maximizing planner rejects the output-maximizing reform, and every percent increase in status envy reduces GDP gains by 0.24%. This illustrates tension between output-based and preference-based efficiency, highlighting how normative definitions shape what it means for an equitable policy to be "efficient" under racial hierarchy.

title: AI Bias for Creative Writing: Subjective Assessment Versus Willingness to Pay
affiliations: Bowdoin College and Bowdoin College

detail.title: AI Bias for Creative Writing: Subjective Assessment Versus Willingness to Pay
detail.abstract: How do perceptions of AI versus human authorship affect engagement with creative work? In an incentivized experiment, participants (N=656) assessed the content of a short story labeled as either human or AI-generated and reported their willingness to pay and work to finish reading it. Consistent with prior research, the AI-labeled story received significantly lower content assessments. However, the time people invest in reading the story and their willingness to pay and work did not differ between the labels, even for the 36% of participants who profess to value human over AI writing. These findings raise questions about whether subjective assessments and stated preferences for human authorship translate into consumer behavior, which has important implications for the effect of AI on employment and consumer surplus.

title: A Notes Bivariate Power Law Processes: Conditional Intensity and Parameter Estimation Techniques
affiliations: Hasanuddin University, Hasanuddin University and Hasanuddin University

detail.title: A Notes Bivariate Power Law Processes: Conditional Intensity and Parameter Estimation Techniques
detail.abstract: The point process model effectively represents the number of random events occurring over time through its intensity function. When events are of two types, a bivariate point process allows simultaneous analysis of each event’s intensity. This study develops a conditional intensity model for a non-homogeneous bivariate point process over time with an event rate approach that follows a certain pattern over time in the form of a time-dependent power law intensity function with two parameters, an initial intensity parameter and a control parameter governing the change in the event rate over time. Parameter estimation is performed using the maximum likelihood method derived from the probability of one event occurring in a very short interval and the non-occurrence at other times. The results of the analysis show that: · The effect of observation duration on model parameters is not linear but depends on its interaction with the pattern of changes in the event rate over time. · The higher the number of events observed, the higher the estimate of the initial intensity of the event. · Both the duration of observation and the timing of events contribute significantly to determining the rate at which the event rate changes over time.

title: The Supreme Court Grants Local Government Autonomy: Where to Go from Here?

detail.title: The Supreme Court Grants Local Government Autonomy: Where to Go from Here?
detail.abstract: The Supreme Court granted the local government in Nigeria with financial autonomy on the 11th of July 2024, allowing the third tier of government to directly receive allocation from the Federation Account. This was a big step towards the autonomy of the local government, but much remains to be done as various obstacles such as interference by the state government, corruption, lack of infrastructure, and inadequate finance continue to pose a threat. Hence, the aim of this study is to highlight the benefits, possibilities, and potential drawbacks of the judicial precedence and likewise to suggest necessary measures that encourage sustainability and local government autonomy. This study adopts a doctrinal methodology; it explores the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (as amended), case laws, local government reforms, and various secondary sources. This study points to the need for a review of the legal and institutional framework of the local government; reforms and innovative policies must be introduced to empower them. In conclusion, the objective is the interest of Nigerian people, and an autonomous local government well equipped to serve Nigeria. To achieve this, the federal government needs to enforce the decision of the Supreme Court and implement a system that encourages the growth of the grassroots of governance.

title: From Market Access to Regulatory Cooperation in the Greater Bay Area (GBA): An International Economic Law Perspective (Asia Pacific Law Review, 2025)
affiliations: Durham Law School

detail.title: From Market Access to Regulatory Cooperation in the Greater Bay Area (GBA): An International Economic Law Perspective (Asia Pacific Law Review, 2025)
detail.abstract: One unique challenge that the Greater Bay Area (GBA) development presents to policymakers is how heterogeneous regulatory frameworks in three different legal jurisdictions within a single sovereign state can be coordinated to facilitate cross-border transactions while respecting the region’s diverse legal traditions. This article argues that, as trade liberalization in goods and services has largely been achieved in the GBA, market access is no longer the primary challenge to its development. Moving forward, regulatory cooperation is a critical factor for the success of the GBA. Deep regulatory cooperation will significantly enhance the business environment, attract domestic and international investors, and strengthen the GBA’s global competitiveness. Moreover, the GBA can draw inspiration from best practices in high-standard regional trade agreements to advance regulatory cooperation.

title: Customs, Trade and Transport Policies in Landlocked Countries: Common Patterns and a Critical Reappraisal
affiliations: Desiderio Consultants Ltd.

detail.title: Customs, Trade and Transport Policies in Landlocked Countries: Common Patterns and a Critical Reappraisal
detail.abstract: This paper examines the customs trade and transport policies of landlocked developing countries (LLDCs), arguing that they should not merely be designed as a uniform reaction to geographical isolation, but used as multifaceted political instruments that can be strategically deployed for multiple purposes, including economic protection, state revenue generation, and political leverage. Using a theoretical framework that integrates trade facilitation, regional integration, and development economics, this study analyzes common policy patterns in LLDCs, including the strategic use of bilateral and regional agreements to ensure the smooth movement of goods, the development of dry ports to expedite goods clearance and attract manufacturing, distribution and logistics services, as well as the establishment of data-sharing systems to optimize logistics flows. Through a comparative analysis of Switzerland, Bolivia, and Ethiopia, we show that the effectiveness of a country's customs, trade and transport policy is fundamentally dictated by its geopolitical context. Switzerland has turned its landlocked status into a competitive advantage by adopting a multifaceted strategy based on strategic integration that combines market openness with a certain degree of protectionism, and a commitment to political neutrality. Furthermore, it has invested in an advanced transport infrastructure, streamlined customs procedures, and implemented a strong intellectual property protection. These policies have been crucial in positioning the country as a highly efficient hub for logistics and manufacturing within Europe serving global markets. In contrast, Bolivia and Ethiopia face significant geopolitical dependencies that profoundly influence their trade and customs policies. We conclude that while LLDCs must embrace openness for survival, they must also maintain a degree of protectionism to shield domestic infant or uncompetitive industries from international competition. Additionally, these nations should cultivate good relationships with neighbors by framing trade and customs policies within their foreign relations, industrial policies and diplomatic strategies. This would allow LLDCs to transform a potential vulnerability (their reliance on neighbors for access to global markets) into a source of diplomatic leverage, by offering neighboring countries concessions in other areas, such as security cooperation, cross-border investment, or shared infrastructure projects, in exchange for more favorable transit terms.

title: A Lawsuit Waiting to Happen: The Use of Non-Financial Metrics by the Investment Industry
affiliations: University of Calgary - Faculty of Law

detail.title: A Lawsuit Waiting to Happen: The Use of Non-Financial Metrics by the Investment Industry
detail.abstract:
This essay is not about whether encouraging the corporate behaviour popularly believed to be reflected in ESG ratings is a good idea, or whether ESG investors succeed in improving corporate behaviour, or even whether investment managers can legally do anything other than seek to maximize their investors’ returns. It is about a very narrow, but crucial question: can investment managers rely on the vast array of third-party ESG ratings, rankings, and indices? Investment managers are fiduciaries of the human beings whose money they control. If an investment manager wishes to use ESG ratings in their investment decision, those ratings need to be accurate. They need to tell the manager something real, something useful, about the rated companies. ESG ratings do not do this.

This essay summarizes a large body of empirical studies investigating ESG ratings. These studies show:

· ESG ratings of the same company vary widely between rating agencies, demonstrating very low validity; 

· ESG ratings do a poor job of predicting future environmental performance, such as the exposure of a company to fines from environmental regulators; 

· ESG ratings of companies do not predict future operating or stock price performance; and

· Corporate disclosure of ESG-favoured information seems connected to less ethical and more self-interested managerial behaviour.

title: Picking Winners or Picking Favorites: Policy Distortion in Taiwan's Camphor Manufacturing under Japanese Colonial Rule (1902-1918)
affiliations: National University of Kaohsiung and Harvard University Department of Economics

detail.title: Picking Winners or Picking Favorites: Policy Distortion in Taiwan's Camphor Manufacturing under Japanese Colonial Rule (1902-1918)
detail.abstract: Picking winners is common among industrial policies, but it is unclear how favoritism affects its aggregate efficiency. This study contributes to broader debates on the limits of "picking winners" through the case of Taiwan's camphor manufacturing industry under Japanese colonial rule (1902-1918). Using firm-level data from the Camphor Monopoly System, we document systematic favoritism: Japanese firms constantly received higher procurement prices and more quota allocations than their Taiwanese counterparts. Taiwanese producers, which were initially less productive, faced harsher evaluation criterion, and this discriminatory treatment forced the exit of less productive firms, leading to rapid convergence of productivity between Japanese and Taiwanese producers. Our dynamic productivity decomposition shows that Taiwanese productivity grew mainly from stringent selection and reallocation, while weaker Japanese firms benefited from leniency. To assess welfare implications, we develop a canonical model of heterogeneous firms with ethnicity-specific productivity distributions and policy treatments. We calibrate the model and show that tightening firm selection for the less productive group distorts resource allocation and ultimately undermines both industry-wide productivity and fiscal revenue by roughly 10%. Our findings underscore a central paradox of industrial policy: while pick-winner strategy may toughen up firm competition within the loser groups, favoritism undermines its aggregate efficiency.

title: The Effect of Censorship on English Language and Narrative Structure in Pakistani Print Media
affiliations: University of Gujrat, Media And Security Research Organization (MASRO), Government Superior Science College, National University of Pakistan and University of Karachi

detail.title: The Effect of Censorship on English Language and Narrative Structure in Pakistani Print Media
detail.abstract: The main objective of this research is to explore the typical linguistic patterns of the censored words in Pakistani print media precipitation and judge the effect of these tendencies on the register and the framing of sensitive issues. The researcher created a large corpus containing every printed English newspaper in Pakistan during the year 2023 along with their magazines. The corpus was then processed through the AntConc tool. The censored words and phrases were listed and categorized. In the present study, five articles, on a daily basis, were chosen from each newspaper using simple random sampling methods and then CDA (Fairclough, 1989) was performed on those articles. The author found that whatever policies followed such as social issues, politics, religion, sexuality, violence and terrorism, national and ethnic issues, and cultural sensitivities, are censored, with some words and phrases repeatedly targeted and limited. The researcher concluded that the nature of censorship constrains speech, restricting not only what is said but also how these matters are discussed, forcing people to choose their words extremely carefully and often express their opinions in hush. It is recommended that the Pakistani print media industry, especially journalists and media organizations should advocate for more freedoms and fewer censors.

title: Protestant Ethics and FinTech Security: Evidence from Marketplace Lending
affiliations: South China Agricultural University and Wenzhou-Kean University

detail.title: Protestant Ethics and FinTech Security: Evidence from Marketplace Lending
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the impact of Protestant culture on the likelihood of fraud collapse of P2P lending platforms. Using platform-level data from 5,085 P2P lending platforms in the Chinese market between January 2008 and October 2019, we find that the presence of nearby churches has a significant negative influence on the incidence of fraud-related collapses in P2P lending platforms. Our results suggest that regions with a strong Protestant cultural influence tend to experience lower risks of fraud-related collapses in the P2P lending market. Moreover, we find that risk-taking and self-discipline can serve as two potential channels through which Protestant culture affects fraud collapse of P2P lending platforms. These findings shed new light on the role of religion and culture as informal institutional alternatives for regulating risks of fraud in Fintech markets.

detail.title: Accounting Guidance for Stock Awards

publicationDetails.journalName: Darden Case Collection

detail.abstract:
This technical note introduces the accounting treatment of employee stock-based compensation, with a focus on awards subject to service, performance, and market vesting conditions. It guides students through the valuation and expense recognition of equity awards under varying contingencies, including complex scenarios involving multiple conditions and tranches. Through clear explanations and practical examples, the note equips readers with the foundational tools to analyze and account for stock-option grants, making it a valuable supplement for courses in financial accounting or executive compensation.

Excerpt

Accounting Guidance for Stock Awards

Many companies choose to supplement their employees' salaries by awarding equity in the form of company shares or options at a specified price. The awards are subject to certain vesting requirements designed to motivate and retain employees.

In its simplest form, the award includes only a time-based contingency so that if an employee remains with the company for a certain period of time, the employee receives a certain amount of stock or options at a specified price. On the day this stock award is approved, the company calculates a fair-value estimate of the award, which is recognized as stock compensation expense on a straight-line basis over the requisite service period, based on the award's vesting requirements.

Example: Darden Company approves a plan on January 1, 20X1, that Employee A will receive 100 stock options if they stay with the company until December 31, 20X5.

In this case, the company calculates the fair value of the stock options as of January 1, 20X1, using similar options in the market or an option-valuation model such as Black-Scholes. That fair value would be recognized on a straight-line basis for the five-year requisite service period. This type of vesting requirement is a service condition: The award vests solely based on Employee A staying with the company for a required amount of time. The requisite service period of five years is explicitly stated in the award.

In addition to the service condition, awards may also include performance conditions (such as a company achieving a specific revenue or EBITDA target) and market conditions (such as a public company reaching a specific market-capitalization [market-cap] threshold). Additionally, awards do not always explicitly state a requisite service period. Requisite service periods might be implied by the terms of the award or be derived through a valuation calculation. Including a performance or market condition complicates the accounting because it is necessary to estimate the likelihood that the contingencies will be achieved.

title: Exploring the Growth Value Equity Valuation Model with Data Visualization
affiliations: Chung Hua University and Tamkang University

detail.title: Exploring the Growth Value Equity Valuation Model with Data Visualization
detail.abstract: The Growth Value Model (GVM) proposed theoretical closed form formulas consisting of Return on Equity (ROE) and the Price-to-Book value ratio (P/B) for fair stock prices and expected rates of return. Although regression analysis can be employed to verify these theoretical closed form formulas, they cannot be explored by classical quintile or decile sorting approaches with intuition due to the essence of multi-factors and dynamical processes. This article uses visualization techniques to help intuitively explore GVM. The discerning findings and contributions of this paper is that we put forward the concept of the smart frontier, which can be regarded as the reasonable lower limit of P/B at a specific ROE by exploring fair P/B with ROE-P/B 2D dynamical process visualization. The coefficients in the formula can be determined by the quantile regression analysis with market data. The moving paths of the ROE and P/B in the current quarter and the subsequent quarters show that the portfolios at the lower right of the curve approaches this curve and stagnates here after the portfolios are formed. Furthermore, exploring expected rates of return with ROE-P/B-Return 3D dynamical process visualization, the results show that the data outside of the lower right edge of the "smart frontier" has positive quarterly return rates not only in the t+1 quarter but also in the t+2 quarter. The farther away the data in the t quarter is from the "smart frontier", the larger the return rates in the t+1 and t+2 quarter.

title: Growth And Value Hybrid Valuation Model Based on Mean Reversion
affiliations: Chung Hua University and Thompson Rivers University

detail.title: Growth And Value Hybrid Valuation Model Based on Mean Reversion
detail.abstract: This article proposes a novel valuation model, growth and value hybrid model, to estimate the stock price. This proposed model combines the essence of the asset-based approach, the income-based approach, and the principle of mean reversion to develop the theoretical closed-form formula consisting of three coefficients: value coefficient, value support coefficient, and growth coefficient. Regression analysis is employed to fit market data to determine these coefficients. Moreover, this study proposes the double sorting method to build the quantile regression models of the formula to estimate the stock price at a specific quantile. The results show that the predictive capability of the hybrid valuation model is superior to the model without using value support coefficient, which supports the assumption that the PBR is not associated with the ROE when the ROE is less than a threshold. In different time periods of the stock market, no significant difference exists on the value support coefficient. However, the variations of the value coefficient and the growth coefficient are significant.

title: Using Mixture Design and Neural Networks to Build Stock Selection Decision Support Systems
affiliations: Tamkang University and Chung Hua University

detail.title: Using Mixture Design and Neural Networks to Build Stock Selection Decision Support Systems
detail.abstract: There are three disadvantages of weighted scoring stock selection models. First, they cannot identify the relations between weights of stock-picking concepts and performances of portfolios. Second, they cannot systematically discover the optimal combination for weights of concepts to optimize the performances. Third, they are unable to meet various investors' preferences. This study aims to more efficiently construct weighted scoring stock selection models to overcome these disadvantages. Since the weights of stock-picking concepts in a weighted scoring stock selection model can be regarded as components in a mixture, we used the simplex centroid mixture design to obtain the experimental sets of weights. These sets of weights are simulated with US stock market historical data to obtain their performances. Performance prediction models were built with the simulated performance data set and artificial neural networks. Furthermore, the optimization models to reflect investors' preferences were built up, and the performance prediction models were employed as the kernel of the optimization models so that the optimal solutions can now be solved with optimization techniques. The empirical values of the performances of the optimal weighting combinations generated by the optimization models showed that they can meet various investors' preferences and outperform those of S&P's 500 not only during the training period but also during the testing period.

title: Endogenous Firm Ownership in General Equilibrium
affiliations: University of Toronto - Rotman School of Management

detail.title: Endogenous Firm Ownership in General Equilibrium
detail.abstract: This paper examines firm ownership structures in competitive general equilibrium by introducing a model where ownership rights emerge endogenously rather than being assumed. By embedding the property rights theory of the firm into general equilibrium analysis, the model demonstrates how market forces determine both initial firm formation by entrepreneurs and subsequent trading of ownership rights. The key finding is that, in equilibrium, firms are created by managers who have long-term importance to performance, but these founder-managers then sell ownership to outside investors. This pattern emerges because managers can capture value through both the sale price and their ongoing employment relationship, while outside owners can only benefit through ownership. The model thus provides a novel theoretical foundation for observed patterns of entrepreneurial exit and reconciles competing approaches to firm ownership in general equilibrium theory. Additionally, it identifies a distinct economic definition of an entrepreneur as an agent whose human capital is valuable for firms even when they do not remain long-term owners. The framework generates insights into firm formation, ownership dynamics, and the nature of entrepreneurship while maintaining the core structure of competitive general equilibrium analysis.

title: The Economic, Demographic, and Institutional Foundations of Trade Liberalization in Pakistan: An Econometric and Machine Learning Analysis
affiliations: National Research University – Higher School of Economics (HSE University)

detail.title: The Economic, Demographic, and Institutional Foundations of Trade Liberalization in Pakistan: An Econometric and Machine Learning Analysis
detail.abstract: Developing economies face persistent challenges integrating into global trade, shaped by complex economic, demographic, and institutional interactions. This study investigates these multifaceted determinants of trade openness in Pakistan from 1990-2024, employing a robust mixed-methods approach that integrates advanced econometrics with machine learning. Unit root tests revealed a mix of stationary and non-stationary series, justifying the use of an Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) model. Cointegration was confirmed via Johansen and ARDL Bounds tests, and an Error Correction Model (ECM) captured dynamics. To address endogeneity, Instrumental Variables (IV-2SLS) and Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) estimators were applied, while machine learning models (LASSO, Random Forest, SVR) explored non-linearities. The results confirm long-run cointegration among trade and its determinants. Gross capital formation (GCF) was a consistently positive and significant driver, though its effect is constrained by limited foreign direct investment. Conversely, human capital deficiencies (proxied by services value-added) showed a significant negative impact, reflecting skills mismatches that limit competitiveness. Institutional quality, particularly government effectiveness, also negatively impacted trade, highlighting governance weaknesses as a major non-tariff barrier. Inflation had a positive relationship with trade, suggesting liberalization may exacerbate price pressures. The ECM indicated a rapid, potentially volatile adjustment to equilibrium. Machine learning (SVR performed best) reinforced the dominance of economic factors like GCF and inflation, while demographic and institutional variables showed weaker contributions, likely due to data limitations. Pakistan's trade is constrained by low human capital, weak institutions, and macroeconomic imbalances, validating an integrated theoretical framework. Policies must boost investment through FDI, enhance education and vocational training to leverage labor abundance, and implement governance reforms to reduce transaction costs. Macroeconomic stability requires coordinated fiscal and monetary policy. This study contributes a novel methodological framework combining econometrics and machine learning, offering a replicable model for analyzing trade dynamics in developing economies. Future research should utilize sectoral data, incorporate sustainability metrics and extend the analysis for comparative regional insights.

title: Parental Perspectives on Social Media's Influence on Student Behavior and Values: Creating MATATAG Curriculum-Aligned Interventions
affiliations: Department of Education: Schools Division Office of Cavite Province, Department of Education: Schools Division Office of Cavite Province and Department of Education: Schools Division Office of Cavite Province

detail.title: Parental Perspectives on Social Media's Influence on Student Behavior and Values: Creating MATATAG Curriculum-Aligned Interventions
detail.abstract:
This study aimed to explore parental perspectives on the frequency, duration, and impact of social media use among Grade 7 students. It examined how parents perceive its influence on their children’s behavior, communication, and values, as well as the strategies they employ to guide and manage online engagement. The ultimate goal was to inform the creation of MATATAG curriculum–aligned interventions that promote responsible and value-driven digital citizenship.

This study used a mixed-methods design, combining quantitative and qualitative data from a validated survey of 333 parents of Grade 7 students at Carmona National High School. The questionnaire gathered both statistical data on social media use and in-depth insights into parental concerns, perceived behavioral impacts, and management strategies. Data were analyzed through frequency distributions for quantitative results and thematic analysis for qualitative responses, with all ethical protocols strictly observed.

Most parents reported that their Grade 7 children use social media daily (74.8%), with significant time spent online—often 1–6 hours per day—making it a deeply ingrained part of their routines. Parents perceived both positive and negative behavioral impacts, such as increased responsibility and improved communication skills, alongside heightened distraction and irritability. Ethical concerns were strongest regarding exposure to inappropriate content, dishonesty, and poor decision-making. In managing online behavior, parents favored open communication, teaching responsibility, and monitoring over strict screen-time limits, reflecting a guidance-oriented approach.

The study concludes that social media is a constant part of Grade 7 students’ lives, offering both opportunities for learning and risks to well-being. Parents and schools must work together to provide intentional guidance that fosters responsible, ethical, and balanced use of technology. Recommendations include integrating a strong digital literacy program into the MATATAG curriculum, training parents, promoting student-led initiatives, and strengthening school policies and support services. Ultimately, these efforts aim not only to prepare students for academic success but to shape their character and values for life in the digital age.

title: Corporate Political Activities and Firms' Carbon Emissions
affiliations: Central Michigan University, University of North Carolina at Wilmington - Cameron School of Business - Department of Economics and Finance, University of Minnesota - Twin Cities - Carlson School of Management and University of Ottawa - Telfer School of Management

detail.title: Corporate Political Activities and Firms' Carbon Emissions
detail.abstract: This study investigates the relationship between corporate political activities (CPA) and a firm's carbon emissions level. We test two competing hypotheses suggesting that political connections either incentivize firms toward stricter environmental standards through reputational pressures or enable higher emissions via regulatory leniency and compromised governance. Utilizing a large sample of U.S. firms, we find robust evidence that politically connected firms have significantly higher carbon emissions. Specifically, adding one politically connected independent director increases absolute emissions by approximately 20% and emission intensity by 16%. These results remain consistent after extensive robustness checks and addressing endogeneity through a stacked difference-indifferences design around director turnover events. We further identify regulatory leniency and weakened environmental governance as mechanisms driving these higher emissions. Cross-sectional analyses reveal that the CPA-emissions relationship is stronger in politically conservative states, financially constrained firms, competitive industries, and complex organizations, whereas institutional investors help mitigate this effect. Our findings highlight how corporate political strategies exacerbate environmental externalities, contributing to the understanding of the broader ecological and societal consequences of firms' nonmarket behaviors.

title: Manuscript Number: JWPE-D-25-04248   Techno-economic Assessment of Engineered Gradient-desalting RO + Evaporation Crystallization Processes for Mine Water: A Filed Study on Shendong Coalfield in China
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Manuscript Number: JWPE-D-25-04248   Techno-economic Assessment of Engineered Gradient-desalting RO + Evaporation Crystallization Processes for Mine Water: A Filed Study on Shendong Coalfield in China
detail.abstract: In China's arid coal belts - where coal-enriched basins overlap with water-stressed regions - coal-mine water emerges as a strategically vital resource for collieries and communities. Optimization of the membrane-thermal hybrid processes was conducted in a two-month field study at coal-mine water plant. Engineered RO-HSRO loop system replaced conventional single-path RO-RO, implementing a salinity-tailored graded desalination with internal cycling to address elevated salinity. This redesign improved anti-fouling and hydraulics via transmembrane concentration control, boosting water-solute separation efficiency at low operational pressures. Processing a 20 m3/h feed (salinity ~ 19.8 g/L), the dual-section reverse osmosis produced 12 m3/h permeate (~ 0.443 g/L) and 8 m3/h concentrate (~ 48.8 g/L). At working pressure 32 bar, switch from RO-RO to RO-HSRO has reduced brine volume by 28.5 % while increasing salinity 1.4-fold to the downstream evaporator. Substituting RO-HSRO for RO-RO cut annual membrane-evaporation OPEX by 18.6% (4.42 vs. 5.43 million CNY) through significant savings on steam, power and chemicals. The gradient circulation strategy provides valuable engineering insights for designing multi-rejection RO systems when treating highly concentrated brines.

title: Reallocating Carbon Responsibility: Does Industrial Restructuring Increase the Burden on Less Developed Regions and Deepen Regional Carbon Inequality in China?
affiliations: Hohai University, Hohai University, Jiangsu University of Science and Technology and Hohai University

detail.title: Reallocating Carbon Responsibility: Does Industrial Restructuring Increase the Burden on Less Developed Regions and Deepen Regional Carbon Inequality in China?
detail.abstract: China's industrial restructuring (2012–2017) yielded a net carbon emissions reduction of 432 Mt (4.6% of 2017 emissions), but these gains were distributed unevenly across regions. Emission cuts were concentrated in certain traditional resource-dependent and coastal provinces, while a few regions saw structural emission increases, reflecting heterogeneous regional outcomes. A signed triadic network analysis reveals significant interprovincial coordination stress and pronounced east–west asymmetries: many emission reductions in the east were achieved by outsourcing carbon-intensive activities to less-developed western provinces, resulting in high-tension configurations. Inequality metrics further underscore this dual outcome. Relative to counterfactual scenarios, the national carbon Gini coefficient declined under restructuring, indicating a moderation of overall carbon inequality. Analyses of the Supply Chain Carbon Inequality Index (CCI) and the Bilateral Carbon Inequality Index (BCI) similarly show that industrial upgrading alleviated some disparities. However, several underdeveloped provinces (such as Xinjiang and Ningxia) experienced rising carbon burdens and deepening disadvantage, as they assumed greater carbon responsibility without equivalent economic gains. Developed eastern provinces were the primary beneficiaries. Overall, restructuring reduced emissions and moderated national carbon inequality, but it increased burdens in some less developed regions, highlighting the challenge of balancing decarbonization with regional equity.

title: Bangladesh’s Ship Recycling Industry in the Global South: Readiness, Regional Competition, and Reform Imperatives
affiliations: Bangladesh Maritime University

detail.title: Bangladesh’s Ship Recycling Industry in the Global South: Readiness, Regional Competition, and Reform Imperatives
detail.abstract: The ship recycling sector in Bangladesh has evolved from informal, beaching-based operations into a globally significant industry—accounting for over 45 percent of world recycling tonnage—and a crucial source of raw materials and employment. This study employs a mixed‐methods design combining secondary data analysis (2014–2024 gross tonnage records), over 500 structured stakeholder interviews (workers, yard owners, engineers, regulators, NGOs, and foreign experts), and ARIMA‐inspired scenario forecasting to 2050. Results reveal critical gaps in Hong Kong Convention (HKC) compliance—around 50% of yards (two dozen) are certified or going two certified—and widespread deficiencies in workplace safety, environmental controls, and institutional enforcement. Comparative benchmarking shows that India has fully modernized over 120 HKC compliant yards through substantial donor and government investment. And Pakistan is rapidly upgrading Gadani with a high value financing package. ARIMA style projections suggest a “business‐as‐usual” baseline of ~2.7 million GT annually to 2050, an optimistic rise to ~5 million GT with green yard expansion, and a pessimistic decline below 2 million GT if reforms falter. Drawing on these findings, five strategic policy pillars are recommended: (1) enact and enforce HKC aligned legislation via a unified regulatory authority; (2) subsidize green infrastructure and institutionalize worker health and safety standards; (3) establish blended financing mechanisms and performance incentives to modernize yards; (4) develop a national recycling information system and fund targeted R&D; and (5) engage regionally and globally to position Bangladesh as a preferred “green” destination under ESG mandates. This study provides a roadmap for Bangladesh to sustain its ship recycling.

title: Top Trading Cycles with Reserve Systems
affiliations: Bowling Green State University and North Carolina State University

detail.title: Top Trading Cycles with Reserve Systems
detail.abstract: School districts often include seat reservations in their school choice assignment process in order to achieve distributional objectives. While the Deferred Acceptance mechanism with seat reservations has been studied extensively, much less attention has been paid to the Top Trading Cycles (TTC) mechanism in this environment. We extend TTC to the environment with reserves by defining the Top Trading Cycles with Reserves (TTC-R) mechanism. We find that the TTCR satisfies the properties that make TTC a desirable option for school choice, namely Pareto efficiency and strategy-proofness. Additionally, we complement our theoretical analysis with an empirical analysis using simulations and find a meaningful efficiency advantage for TTC-R in the most realistic settings for school choice in practice.

title: Complementary Class Activation Maps for Weakly-Supervised Semantic Segmentation
affiliations: Henan Polytechnic University, Henan Polytechnic University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Henan Polytechnic University, Henan Polytechnic University and Henan Polytechnic University

detail.title: Complementary Class Activation Maps for Weakly-Supervised Semantic Segmentation
detail.abstract: The quality of Class Activation Maps (CAMs) is one of the key factors determining the performance of Weakly-Supervised Semantic Segmentation (WSSS) networks with image-level supervision. Vision Transformer (ViT) is becoming the mainstream backbone for image-level WSSS networks due to its ability to avoid the disadvantage of CNN generated CAMs only focusing on discriminative regions in foreground, but the coarse localization maps (Coarse CAMs) generated by ViT suffer from over-smoothing. To address this issue, we have conducted extensive experiments and found that the CAM generated by the patch tokens of ViT encoder are complementary to those generated by multi-head self-attention (MHSA). Based on this discovery, we propose an Adaptive Class-Aware Vision Transformer (ACA-ViT) consisting of a ViT encoder, an adaptive class-aware module, and a class-aware spatial recalibration module for image-level WSSS. Specifically, the ViT encoder first extracts global features of the input image and generates class tokens and patch tokens. Secondly, the adaptive class-aware module utilizes Multi-scale Dilated Convolution (MDC) and Adaptive Class-aware Scoring (ACS) mechanism to solve the spatial over-smoothing issue of the Coarse CAMs, generating object localization maps (patch-CAM) from patch tokens with high response in the target area but partial background activation noise. Finally, the class-aware spatial recalibration module utilizes spatial attention and the ACS mechanism to remove class-independent information from the class-specific CAM extracted by MHSA, generating Class-specific Spatial Recalibration CAM (CSR-CAM) without background activation noise but with uneven target activations. The final Pseudo Mask is accomplished by fusing complementary patch-CAM and CSR-CAM. Extensive experiments have shown that ACA-ViT achieves comparable performance with state-of-the-arts networks in the same category on the PACAL VOC 2012 and MS COCO 2014 datasets.

title: Rupiah Exchange Rate Prediction against the US Dollar Using a Deep Neural Network with a Multi-Output Sliding Window Approach
affiliations: Universitas Muhammadiyah Semarang, Universitas Muhammadiyah Semarang, Universitas Muhammadiyah Semarang and Universitas Muhammadiyah Semarang

detail.title: Rupiah Exchange Rate Prediction against the US Dollar Using a Deep Neural Network with a Multi-Output Sliding Window Approach
detail.abstract: The movement of exchange rates, especially in emerging markets such as Indonesia, often exhibits abrupt and unpredictable fluctuations. Predicting these variations is challenging due to their nonlinear patterns and irregular seasonal effects. While statistical models such as ARIMA and GARCH have long been used in this domain, their ability to capture complex temporal dynamics is limited. Recent developments in deep learning, particularly recurrent architectures like the Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), provide new opportunities for modelling such intricate dependencies.In this study, a multi-output prediction framework is proposed to estimate both bid and ask values of the USD/IDR exchange rate. Historical daily data from 2015–2025 were segmented using a sliding window approach, with additional sine–cosine time encodings to represent weekly cyclical patterns. Three neural architectures—Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), LSTM, and GRU—were trained and assessed using MAPE and R² scores. The GRU consistently delivered the most accurate forecasts (MAPE = 0.0046; R² = 0.9699) and showed strong alignment with actual market movements, particularly during volatile shifts. Dual-target forecasting for both bid and ask exchange rates in a single model.Incorporation of sinusoidal time encoding to capture weekly seasonality.GRU demonstrated superior predictive accuracy and computational efficiency.

reference: Bank of Italy Occasional Paper No. 945
title: The Geography of Innovation: Patent Insights into Europe’s Green and Digital Transitions
affiliations: Bank of Italy and Paris School of Economics (PSE)

detail.title: The Geography of Innovation: Patent Insights into Europe’s Green and Digital Transitions

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of Italy Occasional Paper No. 945
publicationDetails.journalName: Bank of Italy Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Innovation is a key driver of Europe’s green and digital transitions, as well as of its global competitiveness. This report uses patent data from the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) and the European Patent Office to assess where and how technological capabilities are evolving, with a focus on Italy’s position in the European innovation landscape. The analysis reveals persistent cross-country and regional divides, but also signals a shifting global innovation frontier: China has rapidly emerged as a global leader in strategic technologies such as artificial intelligence and green innovation, overtaking the United States, the EU and Japan in international patent filings. This development highlights the need for Europe to reinforce its innovation leadership in high-value, globally competitive domains. Within Europe, Germany leads in both patent volume and quality, while France stands out in artificial intelligence (AI). Italy ranks fifth in patenting overall, with a strong industrial base and targeted specialization in green technologies, yet it grapples with marked regional imbalances and limited public sector involvement. AI patenting in Italy remains concentrated in the industrial North and is led by firms, whereas green innovation is more broadly distributed, offering potential for more inclusive growth. At the same time, the innovation process is becoming increasingly dominated by incumbent firms. The share of new and ‘one-shot’ patenting firms is declining, and the average age of first-time innovators is rising – pointing to structural barriers to entry and the growing complexity of frontier innovation. Stronger support for young, regionally dispersed innovators and complementary investments in adjacent technologies are essential to sustain and expand Italy’s innovation capacity in the context of the Twin Transition.

title: Building Walls, Building Bridges: Border Fortification and Insurgent Influence
affiliations: Princeton University and University of California

detail.title: Building Walls, Building Bridges: Border Fortification and Insurgent Influence
detail.abstract: Militant groups often rely on resources and support that flow across international borders. To disrupt transnational militancy, counterinsurgents regularly fortify their borders. We argue that when border controls restrict their access to external resources, militants compensate by intensifying efforts to cultivate local support. To do so, militants engage in influence and propaganda campaigns aimed at mobilizing civilian cooperation and reinforcing the loyalty of core members. To test this theory we use a two-pronged research strategy that balances identification and generalizability. First, a difference-in-differences design using declassified microdata from Afghanistan offers causal evidence that border fortifications lead rebels to increase locally-targeted propaganda efforts. These efforts deepen civilian perceptions of ideological alignment with militants. Second, we analyze the content of insurgent messaging using an original corpus of militant propaganda. In response to border interdiction, transnational militants target ideologically-inflected propaganda at local audiences, hoping to deepen civilian support and compensate for lost external resources. Our findings cast new light on the adaptive nonviolent tactics rebels employ, and highlight the broader impact of resource shocks on rebel strategy.

title: Does Credit Information Sharing Mitigate Corporate Leverage Manipulation? Evidence from the Construction of the Social Credit System in China
affiliations: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics, Dongbei University of Finance and Economics and Sun Yat-sen University (SYSU) - School of Business

detail.title: Does Credit Information Sharing Mitigate Corporate Leverage Manipulation? Evidence from the Construction of the Social Credit System in China

keywords: The Construction of Social Credit System

detail.abstract: An effective sharing mechanism is key to harnessing the value of social entities' credit information. Using the construction of the social credit system (CSCS) in China as a shock, we find that the enhanced of credit information sharing significantly reduces firms' leverage manipulation. Cross-sectional analyses show that the observed relationship is more pronounced in firms with lower analyst coverage, weaker local bank competition, and lower local fintech adoption. Mechanism analyses suggest that credit information sharing reduces firms' financing constraints and strengthens corporate governance, thereby affecting the cost-benefit structure of leverage manipulation. Overall, these results contribute to our understanding of the critical role of credit information sharing in shaping firms' leverage manipulation behavior.

reference: Bank of Italy Occasional Paper No. 946
title: Embracing the Digital Transition: The Adoption of Cloud Computing and AI by Italian Firms
affiliations: Bank of Italy, Bank of Italy, Bank of Italy and Bank of Italy

detail.title: Embracing the Digital Transition: The Adoption of Cloud Computing and AI by Italian Firms

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of Italy Occasional Paper No. 946
publicationDetails.journalName: Bank of Italy Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: The diffusion of advanced digital technologies is reshaping the organization and performance of firms, yet comprehensive evidence on their adoption remains scarce. This paper draws on data from Banca d’Italia’s business surveys to assess the uptake of cloud computing and artificial intelligence (AI) among Italian firms. As of early 2024, over 50 per cent of firms with at least 20 employees had adopted cloud services, showing minimal variation across sectors and suggesting that this technology is becoming standard infrastructure. AI adoption remains more limited – rising from 4 per cent in 2020 to 13 per cent in 2024 – and tends to be experimental or task-specific. Adoption rates are strongly associated with firm size, export activity, group affiliation, and innovation capacity. Managerial quality and prior digital investments also influence AI uptake. Expectations about generative AI point to job transformation rather than displacement. Accordingly, the analysis reveals that digital technology adoption is positively correlated with realized and expected employment growth.

title: Intermediaries and Asset Prices
affiliations: University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) and University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) - Anderson School of Management

detail.title: Intermediaries and Asset Prices
detail.abstract: Intermediary asset pricing posits that financial institutions are important players in financial markets, and that their decisions shape asset prices beyond simply reflecting the preferences of the average household in the economy. We explain how the intermediary-asset pricing approach helps make sense of empirical patterns in the data: the excess volatility of asset prices, differences in price movements across asset classes, the cross section of expected returns within asset classes, and specific arbitrages and price dislocations. We also review how this view of price fluctuations has important implications for macroeconomic dynamics, international economics, and policy. In particular, the role of financial regulation and monetary policy in alleviating constraints or removing risk from intermediary balance sheets during periods of stress is central in this approach. We highlight both existing progress and gaps for future research.

reference: Bank of Greece Economic Bulletin, Issue 61
title: Housing Affordability for Greek Households
affiliations: Foundation for Economic and Industrial Research (IOBE), Foundation for Economic and Industrial Research (IOBE), IOBE - Hellenic Foundation for Economic and Industrial Research, Bank of Greece and Foundation for Economic and Industrial Research (IOBE)

detail.title: Housing Affordability for Greek Households

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of Greece Economic Bulletin, Issue 61
publicationDetails.journalName: Bank of Greece Economic Bulletin

detail.abstract: In this paper, we use two waves of the cross-sectional Household Finance and Consumption Survey (HFCS) for 2018 and 2021 in order to construct a housing affordability index. The index is based on the ratio of housing costs to household disposable income at both national and regional level, as well as according to the degree of urbanisation. The evolution of the index and of the housing cost overburden rate indicates that housing affordability worsened from 2018 to 2021, while also revealing significant regional heterogeneity, with the issue being more pronounced in urban areas, particularly among renting households. Subsequently, the study identifies, through both descriptive and econometric evidence, the characteristics of the most vulnerable households, showing that younger and smaller in size households, the unemployed and those with lower income are facing the highest affordability constraints. Via these findings, the paper provides useful insights for the design of policies aimed to address the housing affordability issue.

title: Grit in the Gears: Air Pollution and Financial Cognition
affiliations: TEXAS STATE UNIV, Texas State University and Texas State University, San Marcos - College of Business Administration

detail.title: Grit in the Gears: Air Pollution and Financial Cognition
detail.abstract: Financial cognition—the ability to process, evaluate, and act on financial information—is essential for sound decision-making. This paper examines how air pollution influences financial cognition and explores the channels through which this effect may operate. Using high-frequency U.S. county-level data and a two-stage least squares (2SLS) approach with smoke plume intensity as an instrument, we find that higher pollution levels reduce the ability of individuals to detect financial inaccuracies and fraudulent activities, consistent with impaired numerical reasoning and decision-making speed. To distinguish between impaired financial cognition and reduced willingness to engage in financial tasks, we supplement our analysis with a survey experiment. Results show that even short-term exposure to poor air quality lowers financial literacy scores, pointing to a cognitive mechanism rather than disengagement or other noncognitive factors alone. Our results reveal a novel link between environmental quality and household financial engagement, with implications for consumer protection and environmental policy.

title: Analysis of the Aquaculture Methods, Socio-Economic Benefits and Challenges Faced by Small-Scale Fish Farmers in Chiredzi Rural, Zimbabwe
affiliations: University of Johannesburg and University of Johannesburg

detail.title: Analysis of the Aquaculture Methods, Socio-Economic Benefits and Challenges Faced by Small-Scale Fish Farmers in Chiredzi Rural, Zimbabwe
detail.abstract: Aquaculture plays a pivotal role in enhancing food security and socio-economic development, particularly in rural areas. In Chiredzi Rural District, aquaculture is rapidly expanding as a strategy to improve food and nutrition security while enhancing livelihoods and climate resilience. However, there is a significant gap in knowledge regarding the aquaculture methods, socio-economic benefits, and challenges faced by small-scale fish farmers in this region. Therefore, this study aims to analyse the aquaculture methods employed by fish farmers, assess the socio-economic benefits derived from fish farming, and identify the challenges encountered by fish farmers in Chiredzi Rural District, Zimbabwe. A mixed methods approach was used for data collection. Wards and farmers were selected by employing a multi-stage sampling technique. A semi-structured survey questionnaire was administered to 120 fish farmers in three selected wards: Wards 9, 10, and 11. Findings indicate that 85% of farmers utilize earthen pond systems, primarily cultivating Nile tilapia. Aquaculture is currently not a profitable livelihood in Chiredzi rural district but contributes to food and nutrition security. The predominant challenges experienced by fish farmers, include adverse weather conditions, diseases, and insufficient technical assistance. Based on these study findings, we recommend policymakers to prioritize the development of aquaculture in Zimbabwe and recognise its importance for food security and rural livelihoods. Collaborative efforts among government, NGOs, and local farmers are essential to enhance technical support, improve production outcomes, and facilitate market access.

title: Comparisons of Residual Income Model and Growth Value Model
affiliations: Chung Hua University

detail.title: Comparisons of Residual Income Model and Growth Value Model
detail.abstract: Both the Residual Income Model (RIM) and Growth Value Model (GVM) combine the income-based approach and asset-based approach, and blend with the market-based approach, which employs regression analysis and market data to determine parameters in the models. Hence, they have more comprehensiveness than most approaches in the literature. The theoretical and empirical comparisons of RIM and GVM may have profound meaning to stock intrinsic value. The theoretical comparison shows that the ROE-P/B relationship is linear in RIM and power in GVM. When ROE equals the required return rate, whosever P/B is 1.0. When the ROE is small, the P/B estimated by GVM is still greater than 0; however, it may be negative by RIM, which is not reasonable. In a normal range (0~20%) of ROE, the two curves are rather close to each other. The empirical study showed that the GVM can more reasonablly fit the market data, especially when the ROE is rather small or great.

reference: Bank of Italy Occasional Paper No. 943
title: Experiential Financial Education. Assessing the Effectiveness of a Banca d’Italia Museum Exhibition
affiliations: Bank of Italy, Bank of Italy, Bank of Italy, Bank of Italy and Bank of Italy

detail.title: Experiential Financial Education. Assessing the Effectiveness of a Banca d’Italia Museum Exhibition

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of Italy Occasional Paper No. 943
publicationDetails.journalName: Bank of Italy Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We investigate the impact of a museum exhibition on the financial literacy of young people. The exhibition, titled ‘The Adventure of Money’, took place in Rome between October 2023 and June 2024. It offered a preview of Banca d’Italia’s upcoming Money Museum, which aims to stimulate interest in the main events in the history of money and finance. In order to evaluate the effectiveness of the exhibition, we conducted a randomized control trial with about 600 students from 19 Italian upper secondary schools. The results show an improvement in the students’ financial knowledge, as evidenced by an increase of around one third in their initial test scores. The results also show that the exhibition had a greater impact on female students. Finally, no learning decay was observed within the first month following the exhibition.

title: Building Real Estate Valuation Models with Comparative Approach Through Case-Based Reasoning
affiliations: Chung Hua University and Chung Hua University

detail.title: Building Real Estate Valuation Models with Comparative Approach Through Case-Based Reasoning
detail.abstract: The purpose of this study is to propose an innovative real estate valuation approach called Quantitative Comparative Approach, which can estimate correction coefficients to overcome the shortcomings of subjective decisions of correction coefficients of traditional comparative approach. The principle is to assume that the price per unit area of real estate is the average price per unit area of the particular circle of housing supply and demand multiplied by the product of several dimensionless adjustment coefficients of factors. The single regression models of these adjustment coefficients can be built with the stepwise decomposition regression analysis. Then the adjustment coefficients of comparative cases and target case can be estimated with these single regression models, and finally the correction coefficients can be estimated by dividing the adjustment coefficients of target case by those of comparative case. The empirical samples are collected from four circles of supply and demand, and are divided into four data sets. The empirical results show that the Quantitative Comparative Approach is more accurate than the two classical Hedonic price approaches, multivariate regression analysis and neural networks.

reference: Bank of Italy Occasional Paper No. 944
title: La qualità del contesto istituzionale: come varia tra le regioni e nel tempo (The Quality of the Institutional Context: How it Varies Across Regions and Over Time)
affiliations: Banca d’Italia, Bank of Italy and Bank of Italy

detail.title: La qualità del contesto istituzionale: come varia tra le regioni e nel tempo (The Quality of the Institutional Context: How it Varies Across Regions and Over Time)

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of Italy Occasional Paper No. 944
publicationDetails.journalName: Bank of Italy Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
Italian Abstract: In questo lavoro si propone un indice composito di qualità del contesto istituzionale che varia tra le regioni e nel tempo. L’indice tiene conto dei principali domini dell’azione pubblica che influenzano l’ambiente all’interno del quale le imprese e i lavoratori operano: (i) il funzionamento della giustizia; (ii) l’integrità della pubblica amministrazione; (iii) l’efficienza della burocrazia; (iv) la qualità dei servizi pubblici locali. Per coprire questo ampio spettro dell’azione pubblica sono stati raccolti circa 50 indicatori, integrando quelli di natura oggettiva con quelli che riflettono le percezioni di imprese e cittadini. L’analisi mostra che la qualità del contesto istituzionale è peggiore nel Mezzogiorno. Tale risultato, pur essendo diffuso in tutti i domini, è più marcato per la qualità dei servizi pubblici locali che potrebbero risentire, oltre che della minore capacità amministrativa anche dalle minori risorse a disposizione degli enti locali per il loro finanziamento. Il divario non dipende dalla natura oggettiva o soggettiva degli indicatori. Rispetto all’inizio dello scorso decennio, la qualità del contesto è migliorata, soprattutto con riferimento al funzionamento della giustizia civile e all’efficienza amministrativa. Il miglioramento ha riguardato entrambe le aree del paese senza, tuttavia, un apprezzabile processo di convergenza.

English abstract: This paper proposes a composite index of the quality of the institutional context that varies across regions and over time. The index considers the main domains of public action that influence the environment in which firms and workers operate: (i) the functioning of the justice system; (ii) the integrity of the public administration; (iii) bureaucratic efficiency; (iv) the quality of local public services. To cover this broad spectrum of public action, around 50 indicators were collected, combining objective metrics with perceptions of businesses and citizens. The analysis shows that the quality of the institutional context is lower in southern Italy. While this outcome cuts across all domains, it is particularly pronounced in the quality of local public services. This may be due to lower administrative capacity and more limited financial resources available to local authorities. The gap is consistent for both objective and subjective indicators. Since the early 2010s, the quality of the institutional environment has gradually improved, especially with regard to the functioning of civil justice and administrative efficiency. This improvement has affected both the South and the Centre-North of Italy, although no substantial convergence has occurred.

title: Growth Value Two-Factor Model
affiliations: Chung Hua University and Chung Hua University

detail.title: Growth Value Two-Factor Model
detail.abstract: This study developed and tested a stock return prediction model called the Growth Value Two-Factor Model (GVM). The proposed GVM considers beginning and ending book value-to-price ratios (BPRs) and future return on equity (ROE) during a given period. We also used a mean-reverting process to estimate future BPR and ROE, and derived a Growth Value Indicator (GVI) able to help select stocks that deliver better performance. The GVI includes one model coefficient, determined by fitting actual market data. In the GVI, a large coefficient value implies a strong mean-reverting effect on BPR and ROE (i.e., the market is overreacting and stock returns are dominated by the value factor). Conversely, a small coefficient implies a weak mean-reverting effect on BPR and ROE (i.e., the market is under-reacting and stock returns are dominated by the growth factor). The GVM provides a reasonable theory to explain the long-debated issue of whether value stocks or growth stocks provide the best returns. We used Standard and Poor 500 component stocks to examine the effectiveness of the GVM during the period 1998-2008. Conclusions include: (1) value and growth factors are both critical to explaining and understanding stock return performance. As value stocks and growth stocks are not opposites of one another, they should be treated two-dimensionally; (2) BPR and (1+ROE) are clearly affected by mean-reverting phenomena. The exponential-decay mean-reverting model fit well with actual stock data; and (3) GVI performed better than traditional stock selection factors for selecting stocks with better performance, which indirectly demonstrated the effectiveness of the GVM.

title: Female Leaders and Intrahousehold Dynamics: Evidence from State Elections in India
affiliations: Boston College, Northeastern University (USA) and University of Wisconsin-Madison

detail.title: Female Leaders and Intrahousehold Dynamics: Evidence from State Elections in India
detail.abstract: We study the impact of women's political representation on the wellbeing of their female constituents, specifically in the domain of health. Increasing women's political representation leads to greater public provision of reproductive healthcare services in rural areas. Consequently, rural women can exercise greater control over their reproductive choices through the adoption of modern contraception and increased birth spacing. However, these positive impacts are accompanied by an increase in intimate partner violence against women. The increase in spousal abuse is particularly pronounced among women whose husbands prefer to have additional sons, suggesting that the wife's greater contraceptive use triggers marital conflict.

title: The Game of Ranks: A Theory-Driven Critique and a Mechanism for Reform (MSAL)
